=== Deforestation in Indonesia ===
{{Main|Deforestation in Indonesia}}

[[File:Riau palm oil 2007.jpg|thumb|Deforestation in Riau province, Sumatra, to make way for an [[oil palm]] plantation (2007)]]
Indonesia has one of the world's fastest deforestation rates.<ref>{{cite news |title=Selling Out West Papua {{!}} 101 East |date=25 June 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBbVu1ZOpYY&t=114s |publisher=[[Al Jazeera English|Al Jazeera]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="sust">{{cite journal |last1=Limaho |first1=Handoko |author2=Sugiarto |last3=Pramono |first3=Rudy |last4=Christiawan |first4=Rio |date=14 July 2022 |title=The Need for Global Green Marketing for the Palm Oil Industry in Indonesia |journal=[[Sustainability (journal)|Sustainability]] |volume=14 |issue=14 |page=8621 |doi=10.3390/su14148621 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2022Sust...14.8621L}}</ref> In 2020, forests covered approximately 49.1% of the country's land area,<ref>{{cite web |title=Forest area (% of land area) – Indonesia |url=https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/AG.LND.FRST.ZS?locations=ID |access-date=14 June 2021 |publisher=[[World Bank]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251012011255/https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/AG.LND.FRST.ZS?locations=ID |archive-date=12 October 2025}}</ref> down from 87% in 1950.<ref name="landuse">{{cite journal |last1=Tsujino |first1=Riyou |last2=Yumoto |first2=Takakazu |last3=Kitamura |first3=Shumpei |last4=Djamaluddin |first4=Ibrahim |last5=Darnaedi |first5=Dedy |date=November 2016 |title=History of forest loss and degradation in Indonesia |journal=Land Use Policy |volume=57 |pages=335–347 |doi=10.1016/j.landusepol.2016.05.034 |bibcode=2016LUPol..57..335T}}</ref> Since the 1970s, log production, various plantations and agriculture have been responsible for much of the [[deforestation in Indonesia]].<ref name="landuse" /> Most recently, it has been driven by the [[palm oil]] industry,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Austin |first1=Kemen G |last2=Schwantes |first2=Amanda |last3=Gu |first3=Yaofeng |last4=Kasibhatla |first4=Prasad D |date=1 February 2019 |title=What causes deforestation in Indonesia? |journal=[[Environmental Research Letters]] |volume=14 |issue=2 |page=024007 |bibcode=2019ERL....14b4007A |doi=10.1088/1748-9326/aaf6db |doi-access=free}}</ref> which has been criticised for its environmental impact and displacement of local communities.<ref name="sust" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Colchester |first1=Marcus |last2=Jiwan |first2=Normal |last3=Andiko |first3=Martua Sirait |last4=Firdaus |first4=Asup Y. |last5=Surambo |first5=A. |last6=Pane |first6=Herbert |date=26 March 2012 |title=Palm Oil and Land Acquisition in Indonesia: Implications for Local Communities and Indigenous People |url=http://mekongdmp.net/data/Resourcespapers/filepdf/PromisedLand.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531005507/http://mekongdmp.net/data/Resourcespapers/filepdf/PromisedLand.pdf |archive-date=31 May 2012 |access-date=31 May 2012}}</ref>

The widespread deforestation (and other environmental destruction) in Indonesia is often described by academics as an ecocide.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ecocide in Indonesia |url=https://forensic-architecture.org/investigation/ecocide-in-indonesia |access-date=5 July 2023 |website=[[Forensic Architecture]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925122710/https://forensic-architecture.org/investigation/ecocide-in-indonesia |archive-date=25 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Yeo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623130512/https://www.eco-business.com/news/explainer-what-is-ecocide/ |archive-date=23 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last1=Aida |first1=Melly === Chernobyl disaster ===
{{Main|Chernobyl disaster}}

After the disaster, {{convert|4|km2|sqmi|spell=in}} of [[pine]] forest directly downwind of the reactor turned reddish-brown and died, earning the name of the '[[Red Forest]]'.<ref name="bbcmulvey">{{cite news |last=Mulvey |first=Stephen |date=20 April 2006 |title=Wildlife defies Chernobyl radiation |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/4923342.stm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171105054818/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/4923342.stm |archive-date=5 November 2017 |access-date=8 November 2018 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> Some animals in the worst-hit areas also died or stopped reproducing. The disaster has been described by lawyers, academics and journalists as an example of ecocide.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 February 2021 |first=Josef |last=Rybacki |title=Establishing the crime of 'ecocide' |url=https://www.lawgazette.co.uk/practice-points/establishing-the-crime-of-ecocide/5107209.article |access-date=21 June 2023 |website=Law Gazette |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824055620/https://www.lawgazette.co.uk/practice-points/establishing-the-crime-of-ecocide/5107209.article |archive-date=24 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Krogh |first=Peter F. |date=1994 |title=Ecocide: a Soviet legacy |url=https://repository.library.georgetown.edu/handle/10822/552539 |access-date=21 June 2023 |website=Great Decisions 1994 |language=English |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423191027/https://repository.digital.georgetown.edu/handle/10822/552539 |archive-date=23 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojsyk |first=Jakub |date=12 January 2022 |title=Ecocide – the genocide of the 21st century? Eastern European perspective |url=https://www.cirsd.org/en/expert-analysis/ecocide-%E2%80%93-the-genocide-of-the-21st-century-eastern-european-perspective |access-date=21 June 2023 |website=CIRSD |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250817181439/https://www.cirsd.org/en/expert-analysis/ecocide-%E2%80%93-the-genocide-of-the-21st-century-eastern-european-perspective |archive-date=17 August 2025}}</ref>

=== Niger Delta oil pollution ===
{{Main|Environmental issues in the Niger Delta}}

The effects of [[oil exploration]] in the fragile region of [[Niger Delta]] communities and environment have been vast. Local indigenous people have seen little improvement in their standard of living while suffering serious damage to their natural environment.{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}} Some of the hazardous damage of oil and gas exploration in the ecosystem are life-threatening which includes air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution etc.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chinedu |first=Enegide |last2=Chukwuemeka |first2=Chukwuma Kelechukwu |date=2018 |title=Oil Spillage and Heavy Metals Toxicity Risk in the Niger Delta, Nigeria |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6257162 |journal=Journal of Health and Pollution |language=en |volume=8 |issue=19 |doi=10.5696/2156-9614-8.19.180905 |issn=2156-9614|pmc=6257162 }}</ref> Affecting the aquatic lives, human health, also leads to deforestation. According to Nigerian federal government figures, there were more than 7,000 oil spills between 1970 and 2000.<ref>{{cite news |first=John |last=Vidal |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/may/30/oil-spills-nigeria-niger-delta-shell |title=Nigeria's agony dwarfs the Gulf oil spill. The US and Europe ignore it |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161215203635/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/may/30/oil-spills-nigeria-niger-delta-shell |archive-date=15 December 2016 |work=[[The Observer]] |date=30 May 2010}}</ref>

It has been estimated that a clean-up of the region, including full restoration of swamps, creeks, fishing grounds and [[Niger Delta mangroves|mangroves]], could take 25 years.<ref>{{cite news |last=Vidal |first=John |date=1 June 2016 |title=Niger delta oil spill clean-up launched – but could take quarter of a century March 2018 |access-date=14 March 2018 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The Niger Delta is one of the most polluted regions in the world.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Donatus |first=Peter |date=15 October 2016 |title=Shell's Nigeria ecocide is creating a refugee crisis |access-date=6 July 2023 |work=[[Green Left (newspaper)|Green Left]] |language=en |archive-date=3 September 2023 {{Main|Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest}}

[[File:Operação Hymenaea, Julho-2016 (29399454651).jpg|thumb|Deforestation in the [[Maranhão]] state, Brazil]]

|url=https://www.dw.com/en/icc-climate-crimes-suit-filed-against-brazils-bolsonaro/a-59480922 |access-date=10 July 2023 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001160807/https://www.dw.com/en/icc-climate-crimes-suit-filed-against-brazils-bolsonaro/a-59480922 |archive-date=1 October 2022}}</ref> Another has been submitted for ecocide by indigenous chiefs.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Katie |last=Surma |date=24 June 2021 |title=Chiefs demand Bolsonaro's prosecution, say Amazon close to irreversible destruction |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/bolsonaro-should-be-tried-crimes-against-humanity-indigenous-leaders-say-n1272193 |access-date=10 July 2023 |work=[[NBC News]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250924060726/https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/bolsonaro-should-be-tried-crimes-against-humanity-indigenous-leaders-say-n1272193 |archive-date=24 September == International law ==
[[File:20130526234147!US-Huey-helicopter-spraying-Agent-Orange-in-Vietnam b.jpg|thumb|US Huey helicopter spraying Agent Orange in Vietnam.]]
[[File:Olof Palme 1974 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Olof Palme, 1974.]]
[[File:Polly Higgins.png|thumb|Polly Higgins.]]
There is no international law against ecocide that applies in peacetime, but the [[Rome Statute]] makes it a crime to:{{blockquote|
Intentionally launch an attack in the knowledge that such attack will cause incidental loss of life or injury to civilians or damage to civilian objects or widespread, long-term and severe damage to the natural environment which would be clearly excessive in relation to the concrete and direct overall military advantage anticipated.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.envirosecurity.org/news/single.php?id=356 |title=Citizen Campaign to End Ecocide in Europe |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404195940/http://www.envirosecurity.org/news/single.php?id=356 |archive-date=4 April 2019 |website=Institute for Environmental Security |date=22 January 2013}}</ref>}}

The UN's [[International Law Commission]] (ILC) considered the inclusion of the crime of ecocide to be included within the Draft Code of Crimes Against the Peace and Security of Mankind, the document which later became the Rome Statute. Article 26 (crime against the environment) was publicly supported by 19 countries in the Legal Committee but was removed due to opposition from the [[Netherlands]], the [[United Kingdom]] and the [[United States]] of America.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sess.: 1986–1987) |first=UN General Assembly (41st |date=20 January 1987 |title=Draft Code of Offences against the Peace and Security of Mankind :: resolution /: adopted by the General Assembly. |url=https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/124973 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225121210/https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/124973 |archive-date=25 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |date=19 February 2021 |title=Lawyers Are Working to Put 'Ecocide' on Par with War Crimes. Could an International Law Hold Major Polluters to Account? |url=https://time.com/5940759/ecocide-law-environment-destruction-icc/ |access-date=5 July 2023 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705155254/https://time.com/5940759/ecocide-law-environment-destruction-icc/ |archive-date=5 July 2022}}</ref>{{sfn|Gauger|Rabatel-Fernel|Kulbicki|Short|2013|pp=9–11}}

In 1977 the United Nations adopted the [[Environmental Modification Convention|Convention on the Prohibition of Military or any other Hostile use of Environmental Modification Technique]].<ref>[https://treaties.un.org/Pages/ViewDetails.aspx?src=IND&mtdsg_no=XXVI-1&chapter=26&lang=en Convention on the prohibition of military or any other hostile use of environmental modification techniques] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190531033313/https://treaties.un.org/Pages/ViewDetails.aspx?src=IND&mtdsg_no=XXVI-1&chapter=26&lang=en |date=31 May 2019 }}, United nations Treaty Collection</ref> Article I of this Convention says, 'Each State Party to this Convention undertakes not to engage in military or any other hostile use of environmental modification techniques having widespread, long-lasting or severe effects as the means of destruction, damage or injury to any other State Party.' There is no definition of the terms 'widespread, long-lasting or severe'.

In February 2024, the [[European Parliament]] adopted a law making large-scale, intentionally caused, environmental damage 'comparable to ecocide' a crime that can be punished by up to 10 years in prison. Members of the states of the European Union have two years from that date to incorporate their crime into their national laws.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mølgaard Henriksen |first1=Mette |title='Revolutionary': EU Parliament votes to criminalise most serious cases of ecosystem destruction |url=https://www.euronews.com/green/2024/02/27/revolutionary-eu-criminalises-the-most-serious-cases-of-ecosystem-destruction |access-date=28 February 2024 |work=[[Euronews]] |date=27 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251008203018/https://www.euronews.com/green/2024/02/27/revolutionary-eu-criminalises-the-most-serious-cases-of-ecosystem-destruction |archive-date=8 October 2025}}</ref> As of early 2024, there are growing calls to recognize ecocide as an international crime.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Growing calls to recognize 'ecocide' as an international crime in light of Israel-Gaza conflict – EHN |url=https://grist.org/international/israel-gaza-demands-ecocide-international-law/ |access-date=18 April 2024 |website=grist.org |date=26 February 2024 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250831052226/https://grist.org/international/israel-gaza-demands-ecocide-international-law/ |archive-date=31 August 2025}}</ref>

=== Efforts to expand international ecocide law ===
Efforts to criminalise ecocide have sought to include the crime among those prosecuted by the [[International Criminal Court]] established by the [[Rome Statute]]. These crimes include [[genocide]], [[crimes against humanity]], [[war crime]]s and the [[crime of aggression]].<ref>{{cite news |first1=Katie |last1=Surma |first2=Yuliya |last2=Talmazan |date=23 June 2021 |title=The push to make 'ecocide' an international crime takes big step forward |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/push-make-ecocide-international-crime-takes-big-step-forward-n1272059 |work=[[NBC News]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250829071105/https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/push-make-ecocide-international-crime-takes-big-step-forward-n1272059 |archive-date=29 August 2025}}</ref>

In 2010, environmental lawyer Polly Higgins submitted a proposal to the United Nations [[International Law Commission]] that defined ecocide as:<blockquote>The extensive damage to, destruction of or loss of ecosystems of a given territory, whether by human agency or by any other causes, to such an extent that peaceful enjoyment by the inhabitants of that territory has been severely diminished.{{sfn|Higgins|Short|South|2013|p=}}{{page needed|date=December 2025}}<ref name="Jowit">{{cite news |last=Jowit |first=Juliette |date=9 April 2010 |title=British campaigner urges UN to accept 'ecocide' as international crime |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2010/apr/09/ecocide-crime-genocide-un-environmental-damage |access-date=11 October 2015 |work=[[The Guardian]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250929183623/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2010/apr/09/ecocide-crime-genocide-un-environmental-damage |archive-date=29 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Is ecocide a crime? – handlebar-online.com |url=https://www.handlebar-online.com/writing-tips/is-ecocide-a-crime/ |access-date=2 July 2022 |website=handlebar-online.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250819111818/http://handlebar-online.com/writing-tips/is-ecocide-a-crime/ |archive-date=19 August 2025}}</ref><ref>The full proposal, which was submitted to the International Law Commission, is set out in chapters 5 and 6 of {{harvnb|Higgins|2010}}</ref></blockquote>This definition includes damage caused by individuals, corporations and/or the state. It also includes environmental destruction from 'other causes' (i.e. harm that is not necessarily caused by human activity). The purpose was to create a duty of care to mitigate or prevent naturally occurring disasters as well as creating criminal responsibility for human-caused ecocide.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Law |url=http://eradicatingecocide.com/the-law/ |website=Eradicating Ecocide |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160213084617/http://eradicatingecocide.com/the-law/ |archive-date=13 February 2016}}</ref> The proposal has yet to be accepted by the United Nations.{{sfn|Higgins|Short|South|2013|p=}}{{page needed|date=December 2025}}

On 22 January 2013, a committee of eleven citizens from nine European Union countries launched the [[European Citizens Initiative]] (ECI) to 'End Ecocide in Europe'.<ref>{{cite web |title=Initiative details – European Citizens' Initiative |url=http://ec.europa.eu/citizens-initiative/public/initiatives/obsolete/details/2012/000012 |website=[[European Commission]] |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821065752/https://citizens-initiative.europa.eu/initiatives/details/2012/000012_en |archive-date=21 August 2025}}</ref> The initiative aimed at criminalizing ecocide and investments in activities causing ecocide, as well as denying market access to the EU for products derived from ecocidal activities. Three members of the European Parliament, [[Keith Taylor (British politician)|Keith Taylor]], [[Eva Joly]], and [[Jo Leinen]], publicly gave the first signatures.<ref>{{cite web |title=IES > News > Citizen Campaign to End Ecocide in Europe |url=http://www.envirosecurity.org/news/single.php?id=356 |website=www.envirosecurity.org |date=11 August 2015 |access-date=8 November 2015 |language=en-GB |archive-date=4 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404195940/http://www.envirosecurity.org/news/single.php?id=356 }}</ref> The initiative did not collect the one million signatures needed, but was discussed in the European Parliament.<ref>{{cite web |title=Public hearing in the European Parliament {{!}} European Citizens' Initiative {{!}} The ECI Campaign |url=http://www.citizens-initiative.eu/public-hearing-in-the-european-parliament/ |website=www.citizens-initiative.eu |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304122238/http://www.citizens-initiative.eu/public-hearing-in-the-european-parliament/ |archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

In December 2019 at the 18th session of the [[Assembly of States Parties]] to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, [[Vanuatu]] and the [[Maldives]] called for ecocide to be added to the Statute.<ref name="AutoS8-9">{{cite news |last=Siddique |first=Haroon |date=22 June 2021 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jun/22/legal-experts-worldwide-draw-up-historic-definition-of-ecocide |title=Legal experts worldwide draw up 'historic' definition of ecocide |work=[[The Guardian]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005234059/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jun/22/legal-experts-worldwide-draw-up-historic-definition-of-ecocide |archive-date=5 October 2025}}</ref><ref name="asp.icc-cpi.int">{{Cite web |url=https://asp.icc-cpi.int/iccdocs/asp_docs/ASP18/GD.VAN.2.12.pdf |title=Statement by H. E. John H. Licht – Ambassador of the Republic of Vanuatu to the European Union |access-date=15 February 2020 |archive-date=15 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215123120/https://asp.icc-cpi.int/iccdocs/asp_docs/ASP18/GD.VAN.2.12.pdf}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceA">{{Cite web |url=https://asp.icc-cpi.int/iccdocs/asp_docs/ASP18/GD.MDV.3.12.pdf |title=Written Statement of the Republic of Maldives |access-date=15 February 2020 |archive-date=15 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215123119/https://asp.icc-cpi.int/iccdocs/asp_docs/ASP18/GD.MDV.3.12.pdf}}</ref>

In June 2021, an international panel of lawyers submitted a definition of ecocide and proposed a draft amendment to the Rome Statute that would include ecocide among the international crimes prosecuted under the Statute.<ref name="AutoS8-9" /><ref>{{bulleted list|
| {{Cite web |last=Shalev |first=Ariella |date=7 February 2022 |title=Ecocide Law |url=https://www.fdsd.org/ideas/ecocide-law/ |access-date=2 July 2022 |website=Foundation for Democracy and Sustainable Development |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250820064057/https://www.fdsd.org/ideas/ecocide-law/ |archive-date=20 August 2025}}
| {{cite web |url=https://www.irishevs.com/ecocide-making-environmental-destruction-a-crime |title=Ecocide: Making environmental destruction a crime |website=www.irishevs.com |publisher=IrishEVs |date=30 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250819205907/https://www.irishevs.com/ecocide-making-environmental-destruction-a-crime |archive-date=19 August 2025}}
| {{cite news |last=Clark |first=Pilita |date=25 June 2021 |title=Crime of ecocide could transform fight against climate change |url=https://www.ft.com/content/1343dce0-f328-49cc-abc8-2e5060b79eea |work=[[Financial Times]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210625222928/https://www.ft.com/content/1343dce0-f328-49cc-abc8-2e5060b79eea |archive-date=25 June 2021}}
| {{cite news |last=Meredith |first=Sam |date=25 June 2021 |title=Ecocide: How a fast-growing movement plans to put environmental destruction on a par with war crimes |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/06/22/how-a-growing-movement-plans-to-put-ecocide-on-a-par-with-war-crimes.html |work=[[CNBC]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005234048/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/06/22/how-a-growing-movement-plans-to-put-ecocide-on-a-par-with-war-crimes.html |archive-date=5 October 2025}}
}}</ref> The panel included members from the UK, Senegal, the US, France, Ecuador, Bangladesh, Sierra Leone, Samoa and Norway,<ref name="Legal-Def" /> and their proposed definition is:<blockquote>For the purpose of this Statute, "ecocide" means unlawful or wanton acts committed with knowledge that there is a substantial likelihood of severe and either widespread or long-term damage to the environment being caused by those acts.<ref name="Legal-Def" /></blockquote>

=== Notable supporters of ecocide law ===
Many notable people have publicly supported ecocide being made a crime at the International Criminal Court. Several world leaders, environmentalists and celebrities have publicly supported ecocide being made an international crime including [[Pope Francis]], [[António Guterres|Antonio Guterres]], [[Greta Thunberg]], [[Fiamē Naomi Mataʻafa]], [[Emmanuel Macron]], [[Jane Goodall]] and [[Paul McCartney]].<ref name=":14" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Leading states |url=https://www.stopecocide.earth/leading-states |access-date=19 July 2023 |website=Stop Ecocide International |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230719155107/https://www.stopecocide.earth/leading-states |archive-date=19 July 2023}}</ref>

At the 1972 [[United Nations Conference on the Human Environment|UN Conference on the Human Environment]], Swedish Prime Minister [[Olof Palme]] described the damage caused by defoliant [[Agent Orange]] in the Vietnam War as ecocide and called for it to be made an international crime.<ref>{{bulleted list|
| {{Cite web |title=Ecocide: a crime against the planet |url=https://www.lawscot.org.uk/members/journal/issues/vol-66-issue-10/ecocide-a-crime-against-the-planet/ |access-date=22 June 2023 |website=Law Society of Scotland |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250825055725/https://www.lawscot.org.uk/members/journal/issues/vol-66-issue-10/ecocide-a-crime-against-the-planet/ |archive-date=25 August 2025}}
| {{Citation |title=Palme Stockholm Conference 1972 |date=5 August 2012 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0dGIsMEQYgI |access-date=19 July 2023 |language=en}}
| {{Cite news |last=Siddique |first=Haroon |title=Legal experts worldwide draw up 'historic' definition of ecocide |language=en-GB |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jun/22/legal-experts-worldwide-draw-up-historic-definition-of-ecocide |date=22 June 2021 |access-date=22 June 2023 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005234059/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jun/22/legal-experts-worldwide-draw-up-historic-definition-of-ecocide |archive-date=5 October 2025}}
| {{Cite magazine |last=Godin |first=Mélissa |date=19 February 2021 |title=Lawyers Are Working to Put 'Ecocide' on Par with War Crimes. Could an International Law Hold Major Polluters to Account? |url=https://time.com/5940759/ecocide-law-environment-destruction-icc/ |access-date=22 June 2023 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230330015118/https://time.com/5940759/ecocide-law-environment-destruction-icc/ |archive-date=30 March 2023}}
}}</ref> [[Secretary-General of the United Nations|United Nations Secretary-General]] [[António Guterres|Antonio Guterres]] said in 2017 that it is 'highly desirable' to include ecocide as a crime at the International Criminal Court.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 September 2017 |title=Secretary-General's remarks on Global Compact for the environment |url=https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/statement/2017-09-19/secretary-generals-remarks-global-compact-environment |access-date=25 September 2020 |website=[[United Nations Secretary-General]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020181653/https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/statement/2017-09-19/secretary-generals-remarks-global-compact-environment |archive-date=20 October 2020}}</ref><ref name=":14">{{Cite web |title=Supporters of Ecocide Law |url=https://www.stopecocide.earth/supporters |access-date=21 June 2023 |website=Stop Ecocide International |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108124505/https://www.stopecocide.earth/supporters |archive-date=8 November 2023}}</ref><ref name=":25">{{Cite web |last=EFEverde |first=Redacción |date=3 July 2021 |title=Guterres considera que "sería muy deseable" incorporar el Ecocidio como delito en la Corte Penal Internacional |trans-title=Guterres considers that it would be "very desirable" to incorporate ecocide as a crime in the International Criminal Court |url=https://efeverde.com/guterres-seria-interesante-incorporar-el-ecocidio-como-delito-en-la-corte-penal-internacional/ |access-date=21 June 2023 |website=EFEverde |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250927062924/https://efeverde.com/guterres-seria-interesante-incorporar-el-ecocidio-como-delito-en-la-corte-penal-internacional/ |archive-date=27 September 2025}}</ref> [[Pope Francis]] in his address to the [[International Association of Penal Law]] in 2019 stated that 'By 'ecocide' we should understand the loss, damage and destruction of ecosystems of a given territory, so that its enjoyment by the inhabitants has been or may be severely affected. This is a fifth category of crimes against peace, which should be recognised as such by the international community.' He also stated that 'sins against ecology' should be added to Catholic teachings.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 September 2020 |title=Pope Supports Classifying 'Ecocide' as an International Crime |url=https://www.nationalreview.com/corner/pope-supports-classifying-ecocide-as-an-international-crime/ |access-date=16 June 2023 |website=[[National Review]] |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205120524/https://www.nationalreview.com/corner/pope-supports-classifying-ecocide-as-an-international-crime/ |archive-date=5 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=16 September 2020 |title=This movement wants to make harming the planet an international crime |language=en-GB |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/climate-academy/2020/sep/16/ecocide-environment-destruction-international-crime |access-date=16 June 2023 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250904010833/https://www.theguardian.com/climate-academy/2020/sep/16/ecocide-environment-destruction-international-crime |archive-date=4 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Esteves |first=Junno Arocho |date=15 November 2019 |title=Pope Francis: Catechism will be updated to define ecological sins |url=https://www.americamagazine.org/faith/2019/11/15/pope-francis-catechism-will-be-updated-define-ecological-sins |access-date=16 June 2023 |website=America Magazine |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818134753/https://www.americamagazine.org/faith/2019/11/15/pope-francis-catechism-will-be-updated-define-ecological-sins/ |archive-date=18 August 2025}}</ref>

Environmentalist [[Jane Goodall]] supported ecocide being made an international crime, stating: 'The concept of Ecocide is long overdue. It could lead to an important change in the way people perceive – and respond to – the current environmental crisis.'<ref name=":14" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mehta |first=Jojo |date=26 October 2021 |title=Ecocide as an international crime |url=https://una.org.uk/magazine/2021-1/ecocide-international-crime |access-date=2 June 2023 |website=UNA_UK |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251002005015/https://una.org.uk/magazine/2021-1/ecocide-international-crime |archive-date=2 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ecocide Law: The Use of Hard Law to Complement Soft Law |url=https://harvardilj.org/2021/05/ecocide-law-the-use-of-hard-law-to-complement-soft-law/ |access-date=2 June 2023 |language=en-US |archive-date=8 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608141749/https://harvardilj.org/2021/05/ecocide-law-the-use-of-hard-law-to-complement-soft-law/ }}</ref> In 2023, [[Greta Thunberg]], [[Luisa Neubauer]], [[Anuna De Wever|Anuna de Wever]] and [[Adélaïde Charlier|Adélaïde Carlier]] demanded, in an open letter, that all [[European Union]] leaders and heads of state must 'advocate to make ecocide an international crime at the International Criminal Court.'<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yeo |first=Sophie |date=6 November 2020 |title=Ecocide: Should killing nature be a crime? |url=https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20201105-what-is-ecocide |access-date=16 June 2023 |work=[[BBC News]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011070438/https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20201105-what-is-ecocide |archive-date=11 October 2025}}</ref><ref name=":14" /> At the 54th session of the Human Rights Council, [[Volker Türk]], United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights supported ecocide being made a crime at national and international levels.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Türk: Human rights are antidote to prevailing politics of distraction, deception, indifference and repression |url=https://www.ohchr.org/en/statements/2023/09/turk-human-rights-are-antidote-prevailing-politics-distraction-deception |access-date=14 September 2023 |website=[[OHCHR]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231101155211/https://www.ohchr.org/en/statements/2023/09/turk-human-rights-are-antidote-prevailing-politics-distraction-deception |archive-date=1 November 2023}}</ref>

=== Stop Ecocide International ===
Stop Ecocide International (SEI) is an organisation which advocates amending the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court to include ecocide. It works with governments, politicians, diplomats and wider society. The organisation has branches or associate groups in almost 50 countries.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Vargas |first=Ramon Antonio |date=26 September 2022 |title='A powerful solution': activists push to make ecocide an international crime |language=en-GB |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2022/sep/26/activists-push-make-ecocide-international-crime |access-date=19 July 2023 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250819053732/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2022/sep/26/activists-push-make-ecocide-international-crime |archive-date=19 August 2025}}</ref><ref name="Mehta" /> SEI's sister organisation, the Stop Ecocide Foundation convened the Independent Expert Panel for the Legal Definition of Ecocide.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SEF |url=https://www.stopecocide.earth/sef |access-date=8 August 2023 |website=Stop Ecocide International |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005234039/https://www.stopecocide.earth/sef |archive-date=5 October 2025}}</ref><ref name="Legal-Def" />

== History ==
=== 1970s ===
The concept of ecocide originated in the 1970s after the United States devastated the environment in Vietnam through use of [[Agent Orange]] and other herbicides and defoliants during the [[Vietnam War]].<ref name="Watts2" /><ref name="Gray19962" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Minkova |first1=Liana Georgieva |title=The Fifth International Crime: Reflections on the Definition of "Ecocide" |journal=[[Journal of Genocide Research]] |date=2023 |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=62–83 |doi=10.1080/14623528.2021.1964688 |doi-access=free}}</ref> The word was first recorded at the Conference on War and National Responsibility in Washington DC, where American plant biologist and [[bioethics|bioethicist]] [[Arthur Galston]] proposed a new international agreement to ban ecocide.<ref name=Zierler>{{Cite book |title=The Invention of Ecocide |last=Zierler |first=David |publisher=[[University of Georgia Press]] |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-8203-3827-9}}</ref><ref>Article published in New York Times, 26 February 1970; quote in Weisberg, Barry ''Ecocide in Indochina'' (1970) Canfield Press, San Francisco OCLC 135562</ref>

International law professor Richard Falk described the military tactics carried out by the United States in the Vietnam War as a form of 'environmental warfare'.<ref name="Falk 1973 80–96">{{Cite journal |last=Falk |first=Richard A. |date=1973 |title=Environmental Warfare and Ecocide — Facts, Appraisal, and Proposals |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/44480206 |journal=Bulletin of Peace Proposals |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=80–96 |doi=10.1177/096701067300400105 |jstor=44480206 |issn=0007-5035}}</ref> He noted that the level of herbicide spraying, deforestation, and weather modification approached the level of an ecocidal crime. Falk notes how 'the facts have been officially repressed or distorted by the US Government', showcasing the level of political barriers placed to legally prohibit ecocide.<ref name="Falk 1973 80–96" />

Scientific follow-up after the war has been minimal, an assessment conducted in 2021 showcased how only a single wildlife-related study has been conducted since the war occurred; meaning crucial questions about ecological recovery continue to remain unanswered.<ref name="Normile">{{Cite journal |last=Normile |first=Dennis |date=25 April 2025 |title=Did the United States commit 'ecocide'? |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.ady4159 |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=388 |issue=6745 |pages=353 |doi=10.1126/science.ady4159 |pmid=40273270 |bibcode=2025Sci...388..353N |url-access=subscription }}</ref> This significant gap in data has often been identified as significant governmental and academic neglect.<ref name="Normile" />

Despite international outrage, the United States' government have maintained a solid position that the usage of defoliants was a legitimate tactic.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Elia |first=Vincenzo |date=13 August 2025 |title=Ecocide to Effectively Stimulate the Integration of International Environmental and Criminal Laws |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/asian-journal-of-international-law/article/ecocide-to-effectively-stimulate-the-integration-of-international-environmental-and-criminal-laws/8D9918CBC00FB399AE2B169FF67B8F17 |journal=[[Asian Journal of International Law]] |language=en |pages=1–12 |doi=10.1017/S2044251325100702 |issn=2044-2513|doi-access=free }}</ref> This perspective seemed to ensure the problem was framed as a non-permanent, secondary consequence of an important, necessary military action.<ref name="Rawal">{{Cite journal |last=Rawal |first=Shailja |date=1 December 2022 |title=Law and economics behind ecocide: Juggling between rules and standards |url=https://doi.org/10.1177/14614529221107740 |journal=[[Environmental Law Review]] |language=EN |volume=24 |issue=4 |pages=270–287 |doi=10.1177/14614529221107740 |bibcode=2022EnvLR..24..270R |issn=1461-4529|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Thus, this rejected the emerging concept of ecocide.<ref name="Rawal" />

In 1972 at the United Nations [[Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment]], Prime Minister of Sweden [[Olof Palme]] called the [[Vietnam War]] an ecocide.{{sfn|Björk|1996|p=15}} Others, including [[Indira Gandhi]] from India and Tang Ke, the leader of the Chinese delegation, also denounced the war in human and environmental terms, calling for ecocide to be an international crime.{{sfn|Björk|1996|p=}}{{page needed|date=December 2025}}{{sfn|Gauger|Rabatel-Fernel|Kulbicki|Short|2013|p=5}} A Working Group on Crimes Against the Environment was formed at the conference, and a draft Ecocide Convention was submitted into the United Nations in 1973.{{sfn|Björk|1996|p=15}} This convention called for a treaty that would define and condemn ecocide as an international war crime, recognising that "man has consciously and unconsciously inflicted irreparable damage to the environment in times of war and peace."<ref>{{cite book |last=Falk |first=Richard A. |chapter=Environmental Warfare and Ecocide – Facts, Appraisal, and Proposals |editor-last=Thee |editor-first=Marek |title=Bulletin of Peace Proposals |date=1973 |volume=1}}</ref>

The [[International Law Commission]] 1978 Yearbook's {{'}}''Draft articles on State Responsibility and International Crime''{{'}} included: "an international crime (which) may result, inter alia, from: (d) a serious breach of an international obligation of essential importance for the safeguarding and preservation of the human environment, such as those prohibiting massive pollution of the atmosphere or of the seas."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://legal.un.org/docs/?path=../ilc/publications/yearbooks/english/ilc_1978_v2_p2.pdf&lang=EFS |title=Yearbook of the International Law Commission |year=1978 |volume=II, part 2 |website=legal.un.org |publisher=[[United Nations]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824004301/https://legal.un.org/docs/?path=..%2Filc%2Fpublications%2Fyearbooks%2Fenglish%2Filc_1978_v2_p2.pdf&lang=EFS |archive-date=24 August 2025}}</ref> Supporters who spoke out in favor of a crime of ecocide included [[Romania]], the [[Holy See]],<ref name=Article19.3>Sub-Commission on Prevention of Discrimination and Protection of Minorities. Study of the Question of the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide. 4 July 1978. E/CN.4/Sub.2/416, p.124 and p.130</ref> Austria, Poland, Rwanda, Congo and Oman.<ref name=Article19.3 />

=== 1980s ===
The [[Sub-Commission on the Promotion and Protection of Human Rights|Whitaker Report]], commissioned by the [[Sub-Commission on the Promotion and Protection of Human Rights]] on the prevention and punishment of genocide was prepared by then [[United Nations special rapporteur|Special Rapporteur]], [[Ben Whitaker (politician)|Benjamin Whitaker]].<ref>[http://www.preventgenocide.org/prevent/UNdocs/whitaker/ The Whitaker Report] E/CN.4/Sub.2/1985/6.</ref> The report contained a passage that states: <blockquote>Some members of the Sub-Commission have, however, proposed that the definition of genocide should be broadened to include cultural genocide or "ethnocide", and also "ecocide": adverse alterations, often irreparable, to the environment – for example through nuclear explosions, chemical weapons, serious pollution and acid rain, or destruction of the rain forest – which threaten the existence of entire populations, whether deliberately or with criminal negligence.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.preventgenocide.org/prevent/UNdocs/whitaker/section6.htm |title=29-42 Whitaker Report on Genocide |year=1985 |publisher=Prevent Genocide International |website=preventgenocide.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821050053/http://www.preventgenocide.org/prevent/UNdocs/whitaker/section6.htm |archive-date=21 August 2025}}</ref></blockquote>Discussion of international crimes continued in the [[International Law Commission]] in 1987, where it was proposed that 'the list of international crimes include "ecocide", as a reflection of the need to safeguard and preserve the environment, as well as the first use of nuclear weapons, [[colonialism]], [[apartheid]], [[economic sanctions|economic aggression]] and [[mercenary|mercenarism]].'<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://legal.un.org/ilc/publications/yearbooks/english/ilc_1987_v1.pdf |title=1987 Yearbook of the International Law Commission |volume=I |page=56, para 38 |id=A/CN.4/SER.A/1987 |year=1987 |publisher=[[United Nations]] |website=legal.un.org |access-date=11 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722022612/https://legal.un.org/ilc/publications/yearbooks/english/ilc_1987_v1.pdf |archive-date=22 July 2022}}</ref>

=== 1990s ===
In 1996, Canadian/Australian lawyer Mark Gray published his proposal for an international crime of ecocide, based on established international environmental and human rights law. He demonstrated that states, and arguably individuals and organizations, causing or permitting harm to the natural environment on a massive scale breach a duty of care owed to humanity in general. He proposed that such breaches, where deliberate, reckless or negligent, be identified as ecocide where they entail serious, and extensive or lasting, [[Environmental degradation|ecological damage]]; international consequences; and [[waste]].<ref name="Gray19962" />

=== 2010s ===
In 2011, the [[Hamilton Group]] drafted a mock Ecocide Act and then tested it via a mock trial in the [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom|UK Supreme Court]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Walsh |first=Bryan |date=24 October 2011 |title=Is Ecocide a Crime? |url=https://science.time.com/2011/10/24/is-ecocide-a-crime/ |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |access-date=8 November 2015 |issn=0040-781X |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818142648/https://science.time.com/2011/10/24/is-ecocide-a-crime/ |archive-date=18 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ecocide Act {{!}} Eradicating Ecocide |url=http://eradicatingecocide.com/the-law/ecocide-act/ |website=eradicatingecocide.com |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004012143/http://eradicatingecocide.com/the-law/ecocide-act/ |archive-date=4 October 2015}}</ref>

In 2012, a concept paper on the Law of Ecocide was sent out to governments.<ref>[http://eradicatingecocide.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/06/Concept-Paper-Closing-the-Door-to-Dangerous-Industrial-Activity.pdf Closing the door to dangerous industrial activity: A concept paper for governments to implement emergency measures] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304085115/http://eradicatingecocide.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/06/Concept-Paper-Closing-the-Door-to-Dangerous-Industrial-Activity.pdf |date=4 March 2016 }}. The Earth Community Trust.</ref> In June 2012 the idea of making ecocide a crime was presented to legislators and judges from around the world at the World Congress on Justice Governance and Law for Environmental Sustainability,<ref>{{cite news |date=22 June 2012 |last=Johnson |first=Stanley |title=Palm trees and controversy: the world's top judges and lawyers at Rio+20 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/law/2012/jun/22/human-rights-rio-20-earth-summit |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250817161055/https://www.theguardian.com/law/2012/jun/22/human-rights-rio-20-earth-summit |archive-date=17 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Environmental Rule of Law |url=http://www.unep.org/delc/worldcongress/ |website=[[United Nations Environment Programme]] |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130831193509/http://unep.org/delc/worldcongress/ |archive-date=31 August 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Summary of the World Congress on Justice, Governance and Law for Environmental Sustainability, 17–20 June 2012, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil |url=http://www.iisd.ca/uncsd/rio20/unepwc/html/ymbvol203num1e.html |website=www.iisd.ca |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-date=26 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170226223839/http://www.iisd.ca/uncsd/rio20/unepwc/html/ymbvol203num1e.html }}</ref> held in Mangaratiba before the [[United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development|Rio +20 Earth Summit]]. Making ecocide an international crime was voted as one of the top twenty solutions to achieving sustainable development at the [[World Youth Congress]] in Rio de Janeiro in June 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=No lack of solutions at Rio+20 |author=United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development |date=17 June 2012 |url=https://www.preventionweb.net/news/no-lack-solutions-rio20 |website=PreventionWeb |publisher=United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction |access-date=19 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818034335/https://www.preventionweb.net/news/no-lack-solutions-rio20 |archive-date=18 August 2025}}</ref>

In October 2012 the international conference ''Environmental Crime: Current and Emerging Threats''<ref>{{cite web |title=International Conference on Environmental Crime: Current and Emerging Threats |url=http://www.unicri.it/topics/environmental/conference/ |website=www.unicri.it |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-date=14 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230914122449/https://unicri.it/topics/environmental/conference }}</ref> was held in Rome and hosted by the [[United Nations Interregional Crime and Justice Research Institute]] (UNICRI) in cooperation with [[United Nations Environment Programme|United Nations Environmental Programme]] (UNEP) and the [[Ministry of the Environment (Italy)]]. The conference recognized that environmental crime is an important new form of transnational organized crime in need a greater response. One of the outcomes was that UNEP and UNICRI head up a study into the definition of environmental crime and give due consideration to making ecocide an international crime.<ref>{{cite web |title=International Conference on Environmental Crime: Current and Emerging Threats: ACTION PLAN ON COMBATING ENVIRONMENTAL CRIME |url=http://www.unicri.it/topics/environmental/conference/Plan%20of%20action.pdf |website=www.unicri.it |access-date=8 November 2015 |archive-date=1 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160301054531/http://www.unicri.it/topics/environmental/conference/Plan%20of%20action.pdf }}</ref>

In November 2019 [[Pope Francis]], addressing the [[International Association of Penal Law]] (AIDP), called on the international community to recognize ecocide as a 'fifth category of crime against peace.'<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://cnstopstories.com/2019/11/15/catechism-will-be-updated-to-include-ecological-sins-pope-says/ |title=Catechism will be updated to include ecological sins, pope says |date=15 November 2019 |website=CNS top stories |access-date=15 February 2020 |archive-date=30 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830090853/https://cnstopstories.com/2019/11/15/catechism-will-be-updated-to-include-ecological-sins-pope-says/}}</ref>

In July 2019, a group of 24 scientists called for ecocide committed in conflict areas be punished as a [[war crime]].<ref name="Watts2" />

===2020s===
In November 2020, a panel of international lawyers convened by Stop Ecocide International and chaired by British law professor [[Philippe Sands]] and Senegalese jurist [[Dior Fall Sow]] started drafting a proposed law criminalizing ecocide.<ref>{{cite news |title=International lawyers draft plan to criminalise ecosystem destruction |first=OWen |last=Bowcott |url=https://www.theguardian.com/law/2020/nov/30/international-lawyers-draft-plan-to-criminalise-ecosystem-destruction |access-date=1 December 2020 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=30 November 2020 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250817213618/https://www.theguardian.com/law/2020/nov/30/international-lawyers-draft-plan-to-criminalise-ecosystem-destruction |archive-date=17 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Defining 'ecocide': how and why should environmental destruction be criminalised? |url=https://www.leighday.co.uk/news/events/defining-ecocide-how-and-why-should-environmental-destruction-be-criminalised/ |access-date=23 June 2023 |website=leighday.co.uk |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251001194542/https://www.leighday.co.uk/news/events/defining-ecocide-how-and-why-should-environmental-destruction-be-criminalised/ |archive-date=1 October 2025}}</ref>

In May 2021, the European parliament adopted 2 reports advancing the recognition of ecocide as a crime.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Environmental liability rules need revamping |date=20 May 2021 |publisher=[[European Parliament]] |url=https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20210517IPR04121/environmental-liability-rules-need-revamping |last1=Yakimova |first1=Yasmina |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250923072540/https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20210517IPR04121/environmental-liability-rules-need-revamping |archive-date=23 September 2025}}</ref>

In order to enforce implementation and increase citizens' trust in EU rules, and to prevent and remedy environmental damage more effectively, Parliament demands that the [[Environmental Liability Directive 2004|Environmental Liability Directive]] (ELD) and the [[Environmental Crime Directive]] (ECD) be improved.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 May 2021 |title=Environmental liability rules need revamping |url=https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20210517IPR04121/environmental-liability-rules-need-revamping |access-date=2 July 2022 |website=[[European Parliament]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250923072540/https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20210517IPR04121/environmental-liability-rules-need-revamping |archive-date=23 September 2025}}</ref>{{Clarification needed|date=January 2023}}

Also in May 2021 the 179 members of the [[Inter-Parliamentary Union]] (IPU) passed an almost-unanimous resolution inviting member parliaments recognise the crime of ecocide.<ref>{{Cite report |title=Resolution – Parliamentary strategies to strengthen peace and security against threats and conflicts resulting from climate-related disasters and their consequences |date=27 May 2021 |publisher=IPU – 142nd Assembly}}</ref>

The governments of some of the island states at risk from climate change ([[Fiji]], [[Niue]], the [[Solomon Islands]], [[Tuvalu]], [[Tonga]] and [[Vanuatu]]) launched the '[[Port Vila Call for a Just Transition to a Fossil Fuel Free Pacific]]', calling for the phase out [[fossil fuel]]s and the 'rapid and [[just transition]]' to [[renewable energy]] and strengthening [[environmental law]] including introducing the crime of ecocide.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stancil |first=Kenny |date=17 March 2023 |title=Six Island Nations Commit to 'Fossil Fuel-Free Pacific,' Demand Global Just Transition |url=https://www.commondreams.org/news/fossil-fuel-free-pacific |access-date=1 July 2023 |website=[[Common Dreams]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250716103818/https://www.commondreams.org/news/fossil-fuel-free-pacific |archive-date=16 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Fotheringham |first=Caleb |date=22 March 2023 |title=Port Vila call to phase out fossil fuels |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/486463/port-vila-call-to-phase-out-fossil-fuels |access-date=1 July 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |language=en-nz |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251002053928/https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/486463/port-vila-call-to-phase-out-fossil-fuels |archive-date=2 October 2025}}</ref>

On 16 November 2023, European Union legislators reached an agreement on a new directive with jail sentences for the worst polluters and companies fined up to 5% of their global turnover.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kurmayer |first=Nikolaus J. |date=17 November 2023 |title=EU strikes deal on new 'ecocide' rules to put polluters in jail |url=https://www.euractiv.com/section/energy-environment/news/eu-strikes-deal-on-new-ecocide-rules-to-send-polluters-in-jail/ |access-date=4 December 2023 |work=[[Euractiv]] |language=en-GB |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529200949/https://www.euractiv.com/section/energy-environment/news/eu-strikes-deal-on-new-ecocide-rules-to-send-polluters-in-jail/ |archive-date=29 May 2024}}</ref> The agreed law has been formally approved by Parliament in February 2024 and became the Directive on the protection of the environment through criminal law.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Directive (EU) 2024/1203 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 on the protection of the environment through criminal law and replacing Directives 2008/99/EC and 2009/123/EC |url=https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/1203/oj/eng |access-date=2026-04-22 |website=eur-lex.europa.eu}}</ref>

== Domestic law ==
Ten countries have codified ecocide as a crime within their borders during peacetime. Those countries followed the wording of Article 26 of the International law Commission (ILC) Draft which referred to ''intentionally'' causing "widespread, long-term and severe damage to the natural environment" within the context of war – bearing in mind that Article 26 was removed from the final draft submitted to the [[Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court]] in 1996.{{sfn|Higgins|Short|South|2013|p=261}} None of the countries established procedures to measure 'intention'.

The countries with domestic ecocide laws are (in alphabetical order):

* Armenia (2003)
* Belarus (1999)
* Belgium (2023)
* Chile (2023)
* Croatia (2026)
* Ecuador (2008; 2014)
* France (2021)
* Georgia (1999)
* Kazakhstan (1997)
* Kyrgyzstan (1997)
* Mauritius (2026)
* Moldova (2002)
* Russia (1996)
* Tajikistan (1998)
* Ukraine (2001)
* Uzbekistan (1994)
* Vietnam (1990)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Existing Ecocide Laws |url=https://ecocidelaw.com/existing-ecocide-laws/ |access-date=27 November 2023 |website=Ecocide Law |language=en-GB |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721163317/https://ecocidelaw.com/existing-ecocide-laws/ |archive-date=21 July 2024}}</ref>

=== France ===
In 2021, the French National Assembly approved the creation of an 'ecocide' offence as part of a battery of measures aimed at protecting the environment and tackling climate change.<ref>{{Cite news |date=17 April 2021 |agency=[[Agence France-Presse]] |title=France drafts 'ecocide' bill to punish acts of environmental damage |url=https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210417-france-drafts-ecocide-bill-to-punish-acts-of-environmental-damage |access-date=2 July 2022 |work=[[France 24]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250831112114/https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210417-france-drafts-ecocide-bill-to-punish-acts-of-environmental-damage |archive-date=31 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kaminski |first=Isabella |date=26 August 2023 |title=Growing number of countries consider making ecocide a crime |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2023/aug/26/growing-number-of-countries-consider-making-ecocide-crime |access-date=29 July 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250830095223/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2023/aug/26/growing-number-of-countries-consider-making-ecocide-crime |archive-date=30 August 2025}}</ref>

=== Mauritius ===
In 2026, the Mauritian National Assembly amended the Environment Act, giving recognition to the crime of ecocide.<ref>{{cite news |last=Mayer |first=Valentine |date=19 April 2026 |title=Ecocide, the first step towards a fully integrated eco-centric legal framework |url=https://lexpress.mu/node/557358 |work=l'express |location=Mauritius |access-date=29 July 2026}}</ref>

The definition adopted is based, almost word for word, on the legal definition proposed by an independent panel of jurists co-chaired by Prof Philippe Sands QC.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ahmed |first=Najah |date=27 May 2026 |title=Ecocide: when harm to nature becomes a crime |url=https://lexpress.mu/s/ecocide-when-harm-to-nature-becomes-a-crime-558477 |work=l'express |location=Mauritius |access-date=29 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Siddique |first=Haroon |date=22 June 2021 |title=Legal experts worldwide draw up historic definition of ecocide |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jun/22/legal-experts-worldwide-draw-up-historic-definition-of-ecocide |work=The Guardian |location=UK |access-date=29 July 2026}}</ref>
