via Twitter, "We will not be touching your Social Security or Medicare in Fiscal 2021 Budget."<ref name = vox>{{cite news|url=https://www.vox.com/2020/2/10/21131316/trump-2021-budget-entitlement-cuts|title=Trump vowed to not cut Social Security and Medicare — hours before proposing just that|last=Rupar|first=Aaron|date=February 10, 2020|work=[[Vox (website)|Vox]]|access-date=11 August 2020}}</ref> His proposed 2021 budget, unveiled in February 2020, included a $45 billion (~${{Format price|{{Inflation|index=US-GDP|value=45000000000|start_year=2021}}}} in {{Inflation/year|US-GDP}}) cut to the program within Social Security that supports disabled people,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2020/02/12/social-security-trump-budget-aims-cuts-disabled-workers-program/4738795002/|title=Social Security: Here's what Trump's proposed budget could mean for your benefits|last=Picchi|first=Aimee|date=February 12, 2020|work=[[USA Today]]|access-date=11 August 2020}}</ref> as well as cuts to Medicare and Medicaid.<ref name = vox/> In August 2020, as part of a package of executive orders related to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], he signed an order to postpone the collection of the payroll taxes that support Social Security and Medicare, paid by employees and employers, for the rest of 2020. He also said that if he wins re-election, he will forgive the postponed payroll taxes and make permanent cuts to the payroll tax, saying he would "terminate the tax", although only Congress can change tax law.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/us-policy/2020/08/08/trump-payroll-tax-cut/|title=Trump promises permanent cut to payroll tax funding Social Security and Medicare if he's reelected|last=Romm|first=Tony|date=August 8, 2020|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=11 August 2020}}</ref> Analysts said such an action would threaten Social Security and Medicare by eliminating the dedicated funding which pays for the programs.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/dems-say-trumps-payroll-tax-break-weakens-social-security/2020/08/10/b24d5294-db56-11ea-b4f1-25b762cdbbf4_story.html|title=Dems say Trump's payroll tax break weakens Social Security|last1=Alonso-Zaldivar|first1=Ricardo|last2=Taylor|first2=Taylor|date=August 10, 2020|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=11 August 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/08/10/trumps-payroll-tax-cut-would-terminate-social-security-critics-say.html|title=Trump's payroll tax cut would 'terminate' Social Security, critics say|last=Konish|first=Lorie|date=August 10, 2020|publisher=[[CNBC]]|access-date=11 August 2020}}</ref>

===Veterans===
==== 2016 presidential campaign ====
Trump caused a stir in July 2015 when he charged that Senator [[John McCain]] had "done nothing to help the vets," a statement ruled false by PolitiFact and the ''[[Chicago Tribune]].''<ref name="jm">{{cite web|url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2015/jul/21/donald-trump/after-not-war-hero-remark-donald-trump-says-john-m/|title=After 'not a war hero' remark, Donald Trump says John McCain has 'done nothing' for veterans|website=[[PolitiFact]]|access-date=May 30, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/nationworld/politics/ct-trump-veterans-20160529-story.html|title=At Rolling Thunder rally, Trump says those in U.S. illegally treated better than veterans|access-date=May 30, 2016|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=May 29, 2016 }}</ref> Trump added that McCain is "not a war hero. He was a war hero because he was captured. I like people who weren't captured."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/story/2015/07/trump-attacks-mccain-i-like-people-who-werent-captured-120317|title=Trump attacks McCain: 'I like people who weren't captured'|author=Ben Schreckinger|date=July 18, 2015|website=[[Politico]]}}</ref>

As a presidential candidate, Trump was critical of the ways in which veterans are treated in the United States, saying "the vets are horribly treated in this country...they are living in hell."<ref name="jm"/> He favored eliminating backlogs and wait-lists that had caused a [[Veterans Health Administration scandal of 2014|Veterans Health Administration scandal]] the previous year. He claimed that "over 300,000 veterans have died waiting for care."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.politifact.com/virginia/statements/2015/nov/09/donald-trump/trump-says-300000-veterans-dies-waiting-va-care/|title=Trump says 300,000 veterans died waiting VA care|website=[[PolitiFact]]|access-date=May 31, 2016}}</ref> He said he believed Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities needed to be technologically upgraded, to hire more veterans to treat other veterans, to increase support of female veterans, and to create satellite clinics within hospitals in rural areas.<ref name="Veterans Administration Reforms">{{cite web |url=https://www.donaldjtrump.com/positions/veterans-administration-reforms |title=Veterans Administration Reforms That Will Make America Great Again |publisher=Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. |date=October 31, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151031205644/https://www.donaldjtrump.com/positions/veterans-administration-reforms |archive-date=October 31, 2015}}</ref> He proposed a plan for reforming the [[United States Department of Veterans Affairs|U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs]] with provisions to allow veterans to obtain care from any doctor or facility that accepts Medicare, to increase funding for [[Post-traumatic stress disorder|PTSD]] and [[suicide prevention]] services, and to provide [[ob/gyn]] services at every VA hospital.<ref>{{cite web|author=Ali Vitali|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2016-election/donald-trump-gets-specific-veterans-affairs-policy-reform-plan-n455111 |title=Donald Trump Gets Specific on Veteran's Affairs Policy Reform Plan|publisher=[[NBC News]] |date=October 31, 2015}}</ref> Trump called for greater privatization of veterans' care,<ref name="wm">{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/donald-trump-says-he-would-make-va-system-more-privatized-1468273989|title=Donald Trump Says He Would Make VA System More Privatized|last=Kesling|first=Ben|date=July 11, 2016|newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|issn=0099-9660|access-date=July 12, 2016}}</ref> although his plan made no direct reference to letting veterans get health care outside the VA system.<ref name="wm"/> ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' noted that "such a plan is counter to recommendations from major veterans groups, the VA itself and from the Commission on Care, an independent body established by Congress that last week made recommendations for VA changes."<ref name="wm"/> Trump's plan calls "for legislation making it easier to fire underperforming employees, increasing mental-health resources and adding a White House hotline so veterans can bypass the VA and bring problems directly to the president."<ref name="wm"/> Trump opposed the current [[G.I. Bill]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.militarytimes.com/story/military/election/2016/05/09/trump-faces-attacks-veterans-issues/84134896/|title=Trump faces mounting attacks on veterans issues|access-date=July 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822153246/http://www.militarytimes.com/story/military/election/2016/05/09/trump-faces-attacks-veterans-issues/84134896/|archive-date=August 22, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://transcripts.cnn.com/show/nday/date/2016-05-09/segment/03|title=CNN - Transcripts|publisher=CNN|access-date=July 11, 2016}}</ref>

In January 2016, Trump hosted a fundraising rally for veterans (skipping a televised Republican debate to do so). Weeks later, after ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' inquired with the Trump campaign when veterans' groups would receive their checks, the funds began to be disbursed.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/veterans-wait-after-trump-fundraiser-shows-hurdles-for-campaign-1455239053?cb=logged0.7819732998032123|title=Veterans' Wait After Trump Fundraiser Shows Hurdles for Campaign|last1=Kesling|first1=Ben|date=February 12, 2016|last2=Haddon|first2=Heather|newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|issn=0099-9660|access-date=May 30, 2016}}</ref> In April, the ''Journal'' reported that the funds had yet to be fully distributed.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/veterans-charities-await-funds-raised-by-donald-trump-1460069309|title=Veterans' Charities Await Funds Raised by Donald Trump|last=Haddon|first=Heather|date=April 7, 2016|newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|issn=0099-9660|access-date=May 30, 2016}}</ref> In May, NPR confirmed directly with 30 recipient charities that they had received their funds, "accounting for $4.27 million of the $5.6 million total," while the remaining 11 charities did not answer the question.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/2016/05/31/480163943/questions-over-trumps-donations-to-veterans-boil-over|title=At Least $1.9 Million In Donations Trump Collected For Vets Was Sent Last Week|publisher=[[NPR]]|date=May 31, 2016|access-date=2018-12-20|last1=Sprunt|first1=Barbara|last2=Seipel|first2=Arnie|last3=Gonyea|first3=Don}}</ref>

==== Presidency and 2020 campaign ====
In February 2018, the Trump administration initiated a policy known as 'Deploy Or Get Out' (DOGO), ordering the Pentagon to discharge any soldier who would be ineligible for deployment within the next 12 months. This mainly affected disabled soldiers. It also affected [[HIV]]-positive soldiers, who are allowed to serve within the US but cannot be deployed overseas; the DOGO policy meant that they could no longer serve within the US, either.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.intomore.com/impact/breaking-the-trump-administration-is-kicking-hiv-positive-soldiers-out-of-the-air-force|title=BREAKING: The Trump Administration Is Kicking HIV-Positive Soldiers Out of The Air Force|website=intomore.com|date=December 19, 2018 |access-date=2018-12-20}}</ref>

In August 2019, Trump falsely credited himself for passing the [[Veterans Choice Act]], a law that had actually been passed under the previous president, Barack Obama, in 2014.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dale |first=Daniel |date=2020-08-09 |title=Trump walks out of news conference after reporter asks him about Veterans Choice lie he’s told more than 150 times {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/08/politics/trump-veterans-choice-paula-reid/index.html |access-date=2026-10-23 |work=CNN |language=en}}</ref> Trump did sign an expansion of that Act in 2018.<ref name="Aug19C">{{cite web |last1=Dale |first1=Daniel |last2=Subramaniam |first2=Tara |last3=Lybrand |first3=Holmes |date=August 1, 2019 |title=Fact check: Trump makes more than 20 false claims at Cincinnati rally |url=http://lite.cnn.com/en/article/h_13c98257a62ea3e38ab806d6390e16b9 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210215005652/http://lite.cnn.com/en/article/h_13c98257a62ea3e38ab806d6390e16b9 |archive-date=February 15, 2021 |access-date=August 3, 2019 |publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref>

In September 2020, ''[[The Atlantic]]'' reported that Trump referred to Americans who were casualties of war as "losers" and "suckers", citing multiple people who were present for the statements; later reporting by the [[Associated Press]] and [[Fox News]] corroborated some of these stories.<ref name="TA-20200903">{{cite news |last=Goldberg |first=Jeffrey |title=Trump: Americans Who Died in War Are 'Losers' and 'Suckers'|quote=The president has repeatedly disparaged the intelligence of service members, and asked that wounded veterans be kept out of military parades, multiple sources tell The Atlantic.|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/archive/2020/09/trump-americans-who-died-at-war-are-losers-and-suckers/615997/ |date=September 3, 2020 |work=[[The Atlantic]] |access-date=September 4, 2020 }}</ref><ref name="MSNBC-20200903">{{cite news |last1=Maddow |first1=Rachel |last2=LaPorta |first2=James |title=AP report corroborates some stories of Trump deriding veterans - James LaPorta, investigative reporter for the Associated Press, talks with Rachel Maddow about his own reporting that confirms some of the episodes described in an Atlantic article depicting Donald Trump deriding military service and injured veterans. |url=https://www.msnbc.com/rachel-maddow/watch/ap-report-corroborates-some-stories-of-trump-deriding-veterans-91110981648|date=September 3, 2020 |publisher=[[MSNBC]] |access-date=September 4, 2020 }}</ref><ref name="WP-20200904">{{cite news |last1=Itkowitz |first1=Colby |last2=Horton |first2=Alex |last3=Leonnig |first3=Carol D. |title=Trump said U.S. soldiers injured and killed in war were 'losers,' magazine reports |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/trump-said-us-soldiers-injured-and-killed-in-war-were-losers-magazine-reports/2020/09/03/6e1725cc-ee35-11ea-99a1-71343d03bc29_story.html |date=September 4, 2020 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=September 4, 2020 }}</ref><ref name="NYT-20200904">{{cite news |last1=Baker |first1=Peter |last2=Haberman |first2=Maggie |title=Trump Faces Uproar Over Reported Remarks Disparaging Fallen Soldiers - A report in The Atlantic said the president called troops killed in combat "losers" and "suckers." He strenuously denied it, but some close to him said it was in keeping with other private comments he has made disparaging soldiers. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/09/04/us/politics/trump-veterans-losers.html |date=September 4, 2020 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=September 5, 2020 }}</ref><ref name="WP-20200905jb">{{cite news |last=Barr |first=Jeremy |title=Jennifer Griffin defended by Fox News colleagues after Trump Twitter attack over confirmation of Atlantic reporting |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/media/2020/09/05/jennifer-griffin-defended-by-fox-news-colleagues-after-trump-twitter-attack-over-her-confirmation-atlantic-reporting/ |date=September 5, 2020 |access-date=September 5, 2020 }}</ref> Veterans expressed scorn over the report's allegations.<ref name="WP-20200904ta">{{cite news |last=Armus |first=Ted |title='The last full measure of his disgrace': Veterans scorn Trump over report that he calls fallen soldiers 'losers' |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2020/09/04/trump-veterans-atlantic-military-losers/ |date=September 4, 2020 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=September 4, 2020 }}</ref> Trump denied these allegations and called them "disgraceful", adding: "I would be willing to swear on anything that I never said that about our fallen heroes".<ref>{{cite web | title=Trump Denies Report Alleging He Called American War Dead 'Losers' and 'Suckers' | publisher=Independent Journal Review| date=September 4, 2020 | url=https://ijr.org/trump-denies-report-american-war-dead-losers/ | access-date=November 3, 2020}}</ref> [[John Bolton]], who was present at the discussion, also said he never heard Trump make such comments.<ref>{{cite web | last=Deese | first=Kaelan | title=John Bolton says he didn't hear Trump insult fallen soldiers in France | website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]| date=September 4, 2020 | url=https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/515132-john-bolton-says-he-didnt-hear-trump-insult-fallen-soldiers-in-france/ | access-date=November 3, 2020}}</ref>

A fact-check of the topic from ''The Washington Post'' analyzed various statements about the matter and found that, regardless of the nature of the exact quote, Trump has repeatedly expressed negative views about American military personnel who have been captured, wounded, or died in combat. "Trump was puzzled why people went into military service: 'What's in it for them? They don't make any money.' The official added: 'It was a character flaw of the President. He could not understand why someone would die for their country, not worth it.'"<ref name="Kessler_4/22/2024">{{cite news | last=Kessler | first=Glenn | title=The murky facts about Trump's failure to visit American war dead near Paris | newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] | date=April 22, 2024 | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/04/22/murky-facts-about-trumps-failure-visit-american-war-dead-near-paris/ | access-date=June 11, 2024}}</ref>

==== 2024 presidential campaign ====
In August 2024, Trump was criticized for saying that the [[Presidential Medal of Freedom]], which is awarded to civilians, is a "much better" award than the [[Medal of Honor]], the top military honor, because those who are awarded the Medal of Honor "They're either in very bad shape because they've been hit so many times by bullets or they're dead," whereas the recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom is "healthy".<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Kelsey |last2=Ibssa |first2=Lalee |last3=Kim |first3=Soo Rin |date=August 16, 2024 |title=Trump draws fire for remarks about Medal of Honor recipients |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/trump-draws-fire-remarks-medal-honor-recipients/story?id=112883414 |access-date=2024-08-17 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Svitek |first1=Patrick |last2=Lamothe |first2=Dan |date=2024-08-17 |title=Trump draws intense criticism for calling civilian medal 'much better' than military award |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/08/16/trump-medal-of-honor-much-better/ |access-date=2024-08-17 |newspaper=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rahman |first=Khaleda |date=2024-08-16 |title=Donald Trump's Medal of Honor remarks spark anger from veterans |url=https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-medal-honor-remarks-spark-anger-veterans-miriam-adelson-1940135 |access-date=2024-08-17 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref>

==Economy and trade==
{{Main|Economic policy of the first Trump administration|Economic policy of the second Trump administration}}

{{See also|2018 United States federal budget}}

Some of the tax cuts in the [[Tax Cuts and Jobs Act]], which Trump signed into law in 2017, were set by the law to expire in 2025. In April 2024, Trump stated at a fundraiser for wealthy donors that, if returned to office, he would seek to extend those provisions.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.cnn.com/2024/04/10/politics/trump-2017-tax-cuts-rich/index.html| title = Trump tells wealthy donors he wants to extend his 2017 tax cuts. Here's why they'd benefit the most | last = Luhby| first = Tami| date = April 10, 2024|publisher=CNN| access-date = 2024-04-19}}</ref>

===Trade===
{{Further|Tariffs in the first Trump administration|Tariffs in the second Trump administration}}
During his first presidency, Trump withdrew the United States from the [[Trans-Pacific Partnership]], initiated a [[China-United States trade war|trade war]] with China, and negotiated the [[United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement|USMCA]] (United States Mexico Canada Agreement) as a successor to [[North American Free Trade Agreement|NAFTA]] (North American Free Trade Agreement).<ref name="Swanson">{{cite news |last=Swanson |first=Ana |date=July 5, 2018 |title=Trump's Trade War With China Is Officially Underway |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/07/05/business/china-us-trade-war-trump-tariffs.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 26, 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Canada |first=Global Affairs |date=2022-04-21 |title=The Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement |url=https://www.international.gc.ca/trade-commerce/trade-agreements-accords-commerciaux/agr-acc/cusma-aceum/index.aspx?lang=eng |access-date=2022-10-13 |website=GAC}}</ref>

After beginning his second term setting tariffs on specific items like imported cars, lumber, steel and aluminum,<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Guide to Trump's Section 232 Tariffs, in Maps {{!}} Council on Foreign Relations|url=https://www.cfr.org/articles/guide-trumps-section-232-tariffs-nine-maps|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260121000041/https://www.cfr.org/articles/guide-trumps-section-232-tariffs-nine-maps|archive-date=2026-01-21|access-date=2026-02-21|website=www.cfr.org|date=November 14, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> on April 2, 2025—a date he called "[[Liberation Day tariffs|Liberation Day,"]] Trump announced tariffs on every other nation on Earth,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Trump imposes 10 percent universal tariff, higher for top trade partners|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/02/trump-tariff-trade-partners-liberation-day-00267350|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251223133040/https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/02/trump-tariff-trade-partners-liberation-day-00267350|archive-date=2025-12-23|access-date=2026-02-21|work=Politico|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Trump reveals these 2 new types of tariffs on what he calls "Liberation Day," April 2|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/liberation-day-trump-tariffs-explained/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107072820/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/liberation-day-trump-tariffs-explained/|archive-date=2026-01-07|access-date=2026-02-21|language=en-US}}</ref> even on territories that are uninhabited.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-04-03 |title=Trump imposes tariffs on uninhabited Heard and McDonald Islands near Antarctica |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/apr/03/donald-trump-tariffs-antarctica-uninhabited-heard-mcdonald-islands |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212210346/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/apr/03/donald-trump-tariffs-antarctica-uninhabited-heard-mcdonald-islands |archive-date=2026-02-12 |access-date=2026-02-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> When the Supreme Court [[Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump|declared the Liberation Day tariffs to be unlawful]] because of an improper use of emergency powers, Trump pledged to institute a 15% global tariff by different means.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-02-21 |title=President Trump increases global tariffs to 15% after Supreme Court decision |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/president-trump-increases-global-tariffs-to-15-after-supreme-court-decision |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260221231944/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/president-trump-increases-global-tariffs-to-15-after-supreme-court-decision |archive-date=2026-02-21 |access-date=2026-02-22 |work=PBS News |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Cryptocurrencies===
{{See also|Cryptocurrency in the second Trump presidency}}
In 2019, Trump expressed skepticism about cryptocurrencies.<ref name="nbc-crypto">{{cite news |author1=Yen Nee Lee |title=Trump says he's 'not a fan' of cryptocurrencies |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/trump-says-he-s-not-fan-cryptocurrencies-n1029116 |access-date=January 20, 2025 |publisher=CNBC |date=July 12, 2019}}</ref> In a post on Twitter, he said, "I am not a fan of Bitcoin and other Cryptocurrencies, which are not money, and whose value is highly volatile and based on thin air. Unregulated Crypto Assets can facilitate unlawful behavior, including drug trade and other illegal activity".<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=realDonaldTrump |number=1149472282584072192 |title=I am not a fan of Bitcoin and other Cryptocurrencies, which are not money, and whose value is highly volatile and based on thin air. Unregulated Crypto Assets can facilitate unlawful behavior, including drug trade and other illegal activity|date=July 12, 2019|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250119030731/https://x.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1149472282584072192|archive-date=January 19, 2025|url-status=live|author=Donald J. Trump}}</ref><ref name="nbc-crypto"/>

During the 2024 election campaign, Trump became the first presidential candidate to accept digital assets as donations.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hoskins |first1=Peter |title=Melania Trump launches her own cryptocurrency |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c98y47vrv2jo |access-date=January 20, 2025 |work=BBC |date=January 20, 2025}}</ref> He has since, vowed to create a federal "Bitcoin stockpile" from Bitcoins seized by the US government from criminals over time, or by simply acquiring new Bitcoins.<ref>{{cite news |author1=David Yaffe-Bellany |title=A First-Day Trump Order: A Federal Stockpile of Bitcoin? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/16/technology/trump-bitcoin-stockpile.html |access-date=January 20, 2025 |work=The New York Times |date=January 16, 2025}}</ref>

==Environment and energy==
{{Main|Environmental policy of the first Trump administration|Environmental policy of the second Trump administration}}

By March 2016, Trump had not released any plans to combat climate change or provided details regarding his approach to energy issues more broadly.<ref>{{cite web|author=Lauren Carroll|url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2016/mar/01/barack-obama/obama-none-gop-candidates-have-climate-change-plan/|title=Obama: None of the GOP candidates have climate change plan|website=[[PolitiFact]]|date=March 1, 2016}}</ref>

In May 2016, Trump asked Republican U.S. representative [[Kevin Cramer]] of [[North Dakota]]—described by ''[[Reuters]]'' as "one of America's most ardent drilling advocates and [[climate change skeptics]]"—to draft Trump's energy policy.<ref>Valerie Volcovici, [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-trump-energy-idUSKCN0Y41ZP Trump taps climate change skeptic, fracking advocate as key energy advisor], Reuters (May 13, 2016).</ref><ref name="HammEnergy">{{Cite news|author=Michelle Conlin|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-trump-hamm-exclusive-idUSKCN10100Z|title=Exclusive: Trump considering fracking mogul Harold Hamm as energy secretary – sources|date=July 21, 2016|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

===California drought===
{{Main|Droughts in California}}

In May 2016, Trump said that he could solve the [[Drought in California|water crisis in California]].<ref name="NoDrought">{{cite web|author1=Jill Colvin |author2=Ellen Knickmeyer|url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/fea527c86dfe42c78609619c5ce7fd59/trump-vows-solve-californias-water-crisis|title=Trump tells California 'there is no drought'|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=May 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610181100/http://bigstory.ap.org/article/fea527c86dfe42c78609619c5ce7fd59/trump-vows-solve-californias-water-crisis|archive-date=June 10, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He declared that "there is no drought", a statement which the Associated Press noted is incorrect.<ref name="NoDrought" /> Trump accused California state officials of denying farmers of water so they can send it out to sea "to protect a certain kind of three-inch fish."<ref name="NoDrought"/> According to the AP, Trump appeared to be referring to a dispute between [[Central Valley (California)|Central Valley]] farming interests and environmental interests; California farmers accuse water authorities of short-changing them of the water in their efforts to protect endangered native fish species.<ref name="NoDrought"/>

===Climate change and pollution===
{{Main|Pollution in the United States|Climate change|Climate change policy of the United States|Climate change denial}}

Trump rejects the [[scientific consensus on climate change]],<ref name="ParkerDavenport">{{cite news |author=Ashley Parker & Coral Davenport |date=May 26, 2016 |title=Donald Trump's Energy Plan: More Fossil Fuels and Fewer Rules |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/27/us/politics/donald-trump-global-warming-energy-policy.html |url-status=live |url-access=limited |access-date=May 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160526112651/https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/27/us/politics/donald-trump-global-warming-energy-policy.html |archive-date=May 26, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Samenow |first=Jason |author-link=Jason Samenow |date=March 22, 2016 |title=Donald Trump's unsettling nonsense on weather and climate |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/capital-weather-gang/wp/2016/03/22/donald-trumps-unsettling-nonsense-on-weather-and-climate/ |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=May 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322131511/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/capital-weather-gang/wp/2016/03/22/donald-trumps-unsettling-nonsense-on-weather-and-climate/ |archive-date=March 22, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|bX_7dAe280w|Seeing the future of climate policy under the next president}}, September 7, 2016 [[PBS NewsHour]]</ref> repeatedly contending that [[global warming]] is a "hoax".<ref name="MEhren">Ehrenfreund, Max. July 22, 2015. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonkblog/wp/2015/07/22/heres-what-donald-trump-really-believes/ Here's what Donald Trump really believes.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823172902/http://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonkblog/wp/2015/07/22/heres-what-donald-trump-really-believes/ |date=August 23, 2015 }} ''[[The Washington Post]]''.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2016/jan/24/bernie-s/yes-donald-trump-really-did-tweet-climate-change-h/|title=What Donald Trump said about the Chinese inventing the 'hoax' of climate change|website=[[PolitiFact]]|access-date=May 16, 2016}}</ref> He has said that "the concept of global warming was created by and for the Chinese in order to make U.S. manufacturing non-competitive", a statement which Trump later said was a joke.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.businessinsider.com/donald-trump-china-created-climate-change-2016-1 |title=Trump: I was joking when I said the Chinese 'created' the concept of climate change |date=January 8, 2016 |work=[[Business Insider]] |access-date=January 30, 2016}}</ref> It was also observed that he often conflates weather with climate change.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Garza |first=Alejandro de la |date=January 20, 2019 |title=President Trump Renews Climate Change Denial Days After Defense Department Releases Daunting Report on Its Effects |url=https://time.com/5508259/trump-climate-change-defense-department/ |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121005911/https://time.com/5508259/trump-climate-change-defense-department/ |archive-date=January 21, 2019 |access-date=May 28, 2022 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]}}</ref>

Trump criticized President Obama's description of climate change as "the greatest threat to future generations" for being "naive" and "one of the dumbest statements I've ever heard."<ref>{{cite news|author1=Tal Kopan |author2=Heather Goldin|url=http://www.cnn.com/2015/11/30/politics/donald-trump-obama-climate-change-dumbest-thing/ |title=Donald Trump: Obama climate change remarks one of 'dumbest things' uttered in history |date=November 30, 2015 |publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://thehill.com/policy/energy-environment/presidential-races/261619-trump-obama-has-made-us-fools-on-climate-change/ |title=Trump: Obama has made us 'fools' with focus on climate change |date=December 1, 2015 |newspaper=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=January 30, 2016}}</ref> A 2016 report by the [[Sierra Club]] contended that, were he to be elected president, Trump would be the only head of state in the world to contend that climate change is a hoax.<ref name="Sierra Club">{{cite news | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/donald-trump-would-stand-alone-among-world-leaders-sierra-club/ | title=Donald Trump would stand alone among world leaders: Sierra Club | publisher=[[CBS News]] | date=July 12, 2016 | agency=[[Reuters]] | access-date=February 3, 2017 | author=Bernstein, Aaron P.}}</ref> In December 2009, Trump and his three adult children had signed a full-page advertisement from "business leaders" in ''[[The New York Times]]'' stating "If we fail to act now, it is scientifically irrefutable that there will be catastrophic and irreversible consequences for humanity and our planet" and encouraging "investment in the clean energy economy" to "create new energy jobs and increase our energy security".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://grist.org/politics/donald-trump-climate-action-new-york-times/|title=Donald Trump once backed urgent climate action. Wait, what?|first1=Ben|last1=Adler|first2=Rebecca|last2=Leber|date=8 June 2016|work=[[Grist (magazine)|Grist]]|access-date=6 March 2017}}</ref>

Although "not a believer in [[climate change]]", Trump has stated that "clean air is a pressing problem" and has said: "There is still much that needs to be investigated in the field of climate change. Perhaps the best use of our limited financial resources should be in dealing with making sure that every person in the world has [[clean water]]."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/trump-clinton-climate-change-warming-2016-9|title=TRUMP: Claims of global warming still 'need to be investigated'|access-date=October 24, 2016|work=[[Business Insider]] |first=Rafi|last=Letzter|date=August 26, 2016}}</ref>

The Trump administration repealed the [[Clean Water Rule]] protections afforded with the [[Clean Water Act]], which were "established to limit the amount of pollution in U.S. bodies of water and to protect sources of drinking water for about one third of the country."<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 14, 2019 |title=Trump to propose 'narrower definition' for water protection |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/trump-to-propose-narrower-definition-for-water-protection |work=PBS}}</ref><ref name="nytimes repeal">{{cite news |last1=Davenport |first1=Coral |last2=Friedman |first2=Lisa |date=September 19, 2019 |title=Trump Administration Rolls Back Clean Water Protections |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/12/climate/trump-administration-rolls-back-clean-water-protections.html |work=The New York Times}}</ref>

In May 2016, during his presidential campaign, Trump issued an energy plan focused on promoting [[fossil fuel]]s and weakening environmental regulation.<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> Trump promised to "rescind" in his [[First 100 days of the first Donald Trump presidency|first 100 days in office]] a variety of [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]] regulations established during the [[Obama administration]] to limit [[carbon emission]]s from [[coal-fired power plant]]s, which contribute to a warming global climate.<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> Trump has specifically pledged to revoke the [[Presidential Climate Action Plan|Climate Action Plan]] and the [[Waters of the United States#Clean Water Act|Waters of the United States]] rule, which he characterizes as two "job-destroying Obama executive actions."<ref name="ep">{{cite web|url=https://www.donaldjtrump.com/press-releases/an-america-first-energy-plan|title=An America first Energy Plan|publisher=Donald J. Trump for President, Inc.|access-date=May 27, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161203120726/https://www.donaldjtrump.com/press-releases/an-america-first-energy-plan|archive-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref>

Trump has said "we're practically not allowed to use coal any more", a statement rated "mostly false" by [[PolitiFact]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2015/dec/15/donald-trump/donald-trump-exaggerates-how-much-coal-us-has-been/|title=Donald Trump exaggerates how much coal in U.S. has been phased out|date=December 15, 2015|work=[[PolitiFact]]|access-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref> Trump has criticized the Obama administration's coal policies, describing the administration's moves to [[Coal phase-out|phase out the use of coal-fired power plants]] as "stupid".<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> Trump has criticized the Obama administration for prohibiting "[[Coal mining in the United States|coal production]] on [[Federal lands|federal land]]" and states that it seeks to adopt "draconian climate rules that, unless stopped, would effectively bypass Congress to impose job-killing [[Carbon emission trading|cap-and-trade]]."<ref name="ep"/> Trump has vowed to revive the [[Coal mining in the United States|U.S. coal economy]], a pledge that is viewed by experts as unlikely to be fulfilled because the decline of the coal industry is driven by market forces, and specifically by the [[Shale gas in the United States|U.S. natural gas boom]].<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> An analysis by ''[[Scientific American]]'' found that Trump's promise to bring back closed [[coal mines]] would be difficult to fulfill, both because of [[Environmental law|environmental regulations]] and economic shifts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/trump-cannot-bring-back-coal/|title=Trump Cannot Bring Back Coal|last=Lehmann|first=Evan|work=[[Scientific American]] – [[ClimateWire]]|date=May 10, 2016|access-date=August 12, 2016}}</ref> An analysis by Bloomberg New Energy Finance dismissed Trump's claims of a "war on coal": "U.S. coal's main problem has been cheap natural gas and [[Renewable energy|renewable power]], not a politically driven 'war on coal'...[coal] will continue being pushed out of the generating mix."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://archive.thinkprogress.org/coal-wont-rebound-whatever-president-trump-does-energy-experts-say-e30a78745b77/|title=Energy experts give Trump the hard truth: You can't bring coal back|last=Romm|first=Joe|date=2017-02-10|newspaper=ThinkProgress|access-date=2017-02-12}}</ref>

Trump wrote in his 2011 book that he opposed a [[Emissions trading|cap-and-trade]] system to control [[Greenhouse gas emissions|carbon emissions]].<ref>Donald J. Trump ''[[Time to Get Tough|Time to Get Tough: Making America#1 Again]]'' (Regnery, 2011), p. 15.</ref>

According to [[FactCheck.org]], over at least a five-year period, Trump has on several occasions made incorrect claims about the use of [[hair spray]] and its role in [[ozone depletion]]. At a rally in May 2016, "Trump implied that the regulations on hairspray and coal mining are both unwarranted" and incorrectly asserted that hairspray use in a "sealed" apartment prevents the spray's [[Hydrofluorocarbons|ozone-depleting substances]] from reaching the atmosphere.<ref name="Schipani">{{cite web|author=Vanessa Schipani|url=http://www.factcheck.org/2016/05/trump-on-hairspray-and-ozone/|title=Trump on Hairspray and Ozone|website=[[FactCheck.org]]|publisher=[[Annenberg Public Policy Center]]|date=May 30, 2016}}</ref>

In June 2019, the Trump White House tried to prevent a State Department intelligence analyst from testifying to Congress about "possibly catastrophic" effects of human-caused climate change, and prevented his written testimony containing science from [[NASA]] and [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration|NOAA]] from being included in the official [[Congressional Record]] because it was not consistent with administration positions.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/climate-environment/2019/06/08/white-house-blocked-intelligence-aides-written-testimony-saying-human-caused-climate-change-could-be-possibly-catastrophic/|title=White House blocked intelligence agency's written testimony saying climate change could be 'possibly catastrophic'|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/06/08/climate/rod-schoonover-testimony.html|title=White House Tried to Stop Climate Science Testimony, Documents Show|first=Lisa|last=Friedman|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=June 8, 2019}}</ref>

In August 2019, Trump described America's coal production as "clean, beautiful", despite coal being a particularly polluting energy source. Although "[[clean coal]]" is a specific jargon used by the coal industry for certain technologies, Trump instead generally asserts that coal itself is "clean".<ref name="Aug19C"/>

====Opposition to international cooperation on climate change====
{{See also|United States and the Paris Agreement#First withdrawal|United States and the Paris Agreement#Second withdrawal}}[[File:President Trump Makes a Statement Regarding the Paris Accord.webm|thumb|President Trump during his 2017 announcement to leave the international Paris Agreement]]
Trump pledged in his May 2016 speech on energy policy to "cancel the [[Paris Agreement|Paris climate agreement]]"<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> adopted at the [[2015 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] (in which 170 countries committed to reductions in [[carbon emissions]]).<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /><ref name="ReutersInterviewMay172015">{{cite news |first1=Steve |last1=Holland |first2=Emily |last2=Flitter |title=Exclusive: Trump would talk to North Korea's Kim, wants to renegotiate climate accord |work=[[Reuters]] |date=May 18, 2016 |url = https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-trump-exclusive-idUSKCN0Y82JO}}</ref> Trump pledged to cancel the agreement in his first hundred days in office.<ref name="ep"/><ref>{{Cite news|author1=Valerie Volcovici |author2=Emily Stephenson|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-trump-energy-idUSKCN0YH2D9|title=Trump vows to undo Obama's climate agenda in appeal to oil sector|date=May 27, 2016|work=[[Reuters]]|access-date=May 27, 2016}}</ref> This pledge followed earlier comments by Trump, in which he said that as president, he would "at a minimum" seek to renegotiate the agreement and "at a maximum I may do something else."<ref name="FlitterHollandParis">Emily Flitter and Steve Holland, [https://web.archive.org/web/20160519123448/http://uk.reuters.com/article/usa-election-trump-climate-idUKL5N18E5N4 Exclusive: Skeptical Trump says would renegotiate global climate deal], Reuters (May 17, 2016).</ref> Trump characterizes the Paris Agreement as "one-sided" and "bad for the United States",<ref name="FlitterHollandParis" /> believing that the agreement is too favorable to China and other countries.<ref name="ReutersInterviewMay172015" /> In his May 2016 speech, Trump inaccurately said that the Paris Agreement "gives foreign bureaucrats control over how much energy we use on our land, in our country"; in fact, the Paris Agreement is based on voluntary government pledges, and no country controls the emissions-reduction plan of any other country.<ref name="ParkerDavenport" />

Once the agreement is ratified by 55 nations representing 55 percent of global emissions (which has not yet occurred), a four-year waiting period goes into effect for any country wishing to withdraw from the agreement.<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> A U.S. move to withdraw from the Paris Agreement as Trump proposed was viewed as likely to unravel the agreement;<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> according to Reuters, such a move would spell "potential doom for an agreement many view as a last chance to turn the tide on global warming."<ref name="FlitterHollandParis" />

In Trump's May 2016 speech on energy policy, he declared that if elected president, he would "stop all payment of U.S. tax dollars to global warming programs."<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> This would be a reversal of the U.S. pledge to commit funds to developing countries to assist in [[climate change mitigation]] and could undermine the willingness of other countries to take action against climate change.<ref name="ParkerDavenport" />

In August 2016, 375 members of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]], including 30 [[Nobel Prize|Nobel laureates]], issued an open letter warning that Trump's plan to unilaterally withdraw from the Paris Agreement would have dire effects on the fight against climate change.<ref>Ian Simpson [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-scientists-idUSKCN11Q2PD More than 300 scientists warn over Trump's climate change stance], Reuters (September 20, 2016).</ref><ref name="ScientistsLetter">[http://responsiblescientists.org/ An Open Letter Regarding Climate Change From Concerned Members of the U.S. National Academy of Sciences], ResponsibleScientists.org/[[Climate Science Rapid Response Team]] (September 20, 2016).</ref> The scientists wrote, in part:

{{blockquote|[I]t is of great concern that the Republican nominee for President has advocated U.S. withdrawal from the Paris Accord. A "Parexit" would send a clear signal to the rest of the world: "The United States does not care about the global problem of human-caused climate change. You are on your own." Such a decision would make it far more difficult to develop effective global strategies for mitigating and adapting to climate change. The consequences of opting out of the global community would be severe and long-lasting – for our planet's climate and for the international credibility of the United States.<ref name="ScientistsLetter"/>}}

===Energy independence===
{{Main|United States energy independence}}

In his May 2016 speech on energy policy, Trump stated: "Under my presidency, we will accomplish complete American [[energy independence]]. We will become totally independent of the need to import energy from the oil cartel or any nation hostile to our interest."<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that "experts say that such remarks display a basic ignorance of the workings of the global oil markets."<ref name="ParkerDavenport" />

===Environmental regulation===
In January 2016, Trump vowed "tremendous cutting" of the budget for the [[U.S. Environmental Protection Agency]] if elected.<ref name="epa-funding">{{cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/donald-trump-vows-to-slash-funding-for-education-epa-1452551107 |title=Donald Trump Vows to Slash Funding for Education, EPA |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |first=Heather |last=Haddon |date=January 11, 2016}}</ref> In an October 2015 interview with [[Chris Wallace]], Trump explained, "what they do is a disgrace. Every week they come out with new regulations."<ref name="cw">{{cite web|url=http://www.realclearpolitics.com/video/2015/10/18/full_replay_and_transcript_donald_trump_with_fncs_chris_wallace.html|title=Full Interview and Transcript: Donald Trump on "FOX News Sunday" With Chris Wallace|website=realclearpolitics.com|access-date=May 22, 2016}}</ref> When Wallace asked, "Who's going to protect the environment?", Trump answered "we'll be fine with the environment. We can leave a little bit, but you can't destroy businesses."<ref name="cw"/>

Trump has charged that the "[[United States Fish and Wildlife Service|U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service]] abuses the [[Endangered Species Act]] to restrict oil and gas exploration."<ref name="ep"/> In 2011, Trump said that would permit drilling in the [[Arctic National Wildlife Refuge]] in northeastern [[Alaska]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxnews.com/transcript/exclusive-donald-trump-talks-2012-calls-obama-the-worst-president-ever|title=Exclusive: Donald Trump Talks 2012, Calls Obama the 'Worst President Ever'|date=June 16, 2016|publisher=[[Fox News]]|access-date=June 16, 2016}}</ref>

In July 2016, Trump suggested that he was in favor of state and local bans on hydraulic fracturing ([[fracking]]), saying, "I'm in favor of fracking, but I think that voters should have a big say in it. I mean, there's some areas, maybe, they don't want to have fracking. And I think if the voters are voting for it, that's up to them...if a municipality or a state wants to ban fracking, I can understand that."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thehill.com/policy/energy-environment/289851-trump-let-towns-states-ban-fracking/|title=Trump indicates towns, states should be able to ban fracking|last=Rupert|first=Evelyn|work=The Hill |date=July 29, 2016|access-date=July 30, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehill.com/policy/energy-environment/290186-trump-rattles-industry-with-fracking-position/|title=Trump rattles industry with fracking position|access-date=October 24, 2016|work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|first=Timothy|last=Cama|date=August 3, 2016}}</ref>

===Pipelines===
====Keystone XL====
{{Main|Keystone Pipeline}}

Trump promised to construct the Keystone XL pipeline, a proposed project to bring [[Petroleum industry in Canada|Canadian petroleum]] to the U.S.<ref name="ParkerDavenport" /> Trump pledged that if elected, he would ask [[TransCanada Corporation|TransCanada Corp.]] to renew its permit application for the project within his first hundred days in office.<ref name="ep"/> Trump claimed that Keystone XL pipeline will have "no impact on environment" and create "lots of jobs for U.S.",<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2015/08/18/politics/donald-trump-keystone-pipeline-support/index.html|title=Donald Trump supports the Keystone pipeline|first=Theodore |last=Schleifer|publisher=[[CNN]]|access-date=June 16, 2016}}</ref> although in fact the pipeline is projected to create only 35 permanent jobs.<ref>Katie Sanders, [http://www.politifact.com/punditfact/statements/2014/feb/10/van-jones/cnns-van-jones-says-keystone-pipeline-only-creates/ CNN's Van Jones says Keystone pipeline only creates 35 permanent jobs], PolitiFact (February 10, 2014).</ref>

In his first days in office, Trump revived the Keystone XL project, signing a [[presidential memorandum]] reversing the rejection of the proposed pipeline that President Obama had made. Trump "also signed a directive ordering an end to protracted environmental reviews," pledging to make environmental review " a very short process".<ref>Peter Baker & Coral Davenport, [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/01/24/us/politics/keystone-dakota-pipeline-trump.html Trump Revives Keystone Pipeline Rejected by Obama], ''[[The New York Times]]'' (January 24, 2017).</ref>

====Dakota Access Pipeline====
{{Main|Dakota Access Pipeline|Dakota Access Pipeline protests}}

After months of protest by thousands of protesters, including the largest gathering of [[Native Americans in the United States|Native Americans]] in 100 years, in December 2016 the [[United States Army Corps of Engineers]] under the Obama administration announced that it would not grant an [[easement]] for the pipeline, and the Corps of Engineers undertook an [[environmental impact statement]] to look at possible alternative routes.<ref name="cnn.com2">{{Cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2016/12/04/politics/dakota-access-pipeline/|title=Dakota Access Pipeline to be rerouted|date=2016-12-04|access-date=2018-02-22|publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref>
However, in February 2017, newly elected President Donald Trump ended the environmental impact assessment and ordered construction to continue.<ref name="NPR">{{Cite news |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2017/02/07/513951600/army-approves-dakota-access-pipeline-route-paving-way-for-the-projects-completio |title=Army Approves Dakota Access Pipeline Route, Paving Way For The Project's Completion |last=Hersher |first=Rebecca |date=February 22, 2018}}</ref> Trump has financial ties to [[Energy Transfer Partners]] and [[Phillips 66]], who are both directly involved in the controversial project. The CEO of Energy Transfer Partners is a campaign donor for Donald Trump.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Milman|first1=Oliver|title=Dakota Access pipeline company and Donald Trump have close financial ties|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2016/oct/26/donald-trump-dakota-access-pipeline-investment-energy-transfer-partners|website=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=November 2, 2016|date=October 26, 2016}}</ref>

===Renewable energy===
{{Main|Renewable energy in the United States|Environmental policy of the second Trump administration#Solar and wind power|Environmental policy of the first Trump administration#Renewable energy policy}}
{{Further|Trump International Golf Club Scotland Ltd v The Scottish Ministers}}
In 2006, Trump expressed concerns about a wind farm planned to be built near where he planned to build a golf course.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2006-05-24 |title=Fears over Trump's golfing plans |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/north_east/5008624.stm |access-date=2026-04-03 |work=BBC |language=en-GB}}</ref> After the plans for the 11 wind turbines were approved by the Scottish government, Trump unsuccessfully sued in the [[Court of Session|Court of Sessions]] to have the plan declared illegal.<ref name="stv05062015">{{cite web |date=5 June 2015 |title=Billionaire Donald Trump loses legal battle over offshore wind farm |url=http://news.stv.tv/north/1322381-donald-trump-loses-battle-over-aberdeen-bay-wind-farm-near-golf-course/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304090145/http://news.stv.tv/north/1322381-donald-trump-loses-battle-over-aberdeen-bay-wind-farm-near-golf-course/ |archive-date=4 March 2016 |access-date=21 July 2016 |website=[[STV (TV channel)|STV]]}}</ref> Trump unsuccessfully appealed the case to the [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom|UK Supreme Court]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=John |first=Tara |title=Donald Trump’s Fight Against Windfarm Defeated by the U.K. Supreme Court |url=https://time.com/4151145/donald-trumps-uk-supreme-court/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714111343/https://time.com/4151145/donald-trumps-uk-supreme-court/ |archive-date=2025-07-14 |access-date=2026-04-03 |work=TIME |language=en}}</ref> Trump made 60 [[Tweet (social media)|tweets]] about the offshore wind farm from 2012 to 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-11-22 |title=Trump tweeted about Scottish wind farm 60 times |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2016/11/trump-scottish-wind-farms-231741 |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref>

In his 2015 book ''[[Crippled America]]'', Trump is highly critical of the "big push" to develop renewable energy, arguing that the push is based on a mistaken belief that greenhouse gases contribute to climate change.<ref name="ca">{{cite web|url=http://www.ontheissues.org/Archive/Crippled_America_Energy_+_Oil.htm|title=Crippled America, by Donald J. Trump (Sept. 2015)|website=ontheissues.org|access-date=June 4, 2016}}</ref> It says, "There has been a big push to develop alternative forms of energy—so-called green energy—from renewable sources. That's a big mistake. To begin with, the whole push for renewable energy is being driven by the wrong motivation, the mistaken belief that global climate change is being caused by carbon emissions. If you don't buy that—and I don't—then what we have is really just an expensive way of making the tree-huggers feel good about themselves."<ref name="ca"/>

Trump uses the incorrect term for wind turbines, calling them [[Windmill|windmills]].<ref name="fs">{{Cite web |title=The Windmills in Donald Trump's Mind |url=https://www.mcgill.ca/oss/article/critical-thinking-general-science-climate-change/windmills-donald-trumps-mind |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=McGill Office for Science and Society |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Peters |first=Adele |date=January 22, 2025 |title=Why Donald Trump hates wind power |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91264701/why-donald-trump-hates-wind-power |access-date=April 3, 2026 |work=[[Fast Company]]}}</ref> Trump's position on wind turbines has been compared to [[Don Quixote]] due to the character tilting at windmills because he thought they were giants.<ref name="fs"/><ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-08-15 |title=The story of Donald Trump’s feud with his one true nemesis: Windmills |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/the-story-of-donald-trumps-feud-with-his-one-true-nemesis-windmills/2019/08/15/f637980a-be9e-11e9-b873-63ace636af08_story.html |access-date=2026-04-03 |work=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

Trump has made several false claims about wind turbines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDonald |first=Jessica |date=2019-04-04 |title=Trump's Faulty Wind Power Claims |url=https://www.factcheck.org/2019/04/trumps-faulty-wind-power-claims/ |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=FactCheck.org |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Steffen |first=Sarah |date=June 7, 2025 |title=Fact check: Debunking Trump's false claims on wind energy |url=https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-debunking-trumps-false-claims-on-wind-energy/a-72824310 |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=Deutsche Welle |language=en}}</ref> Trump finds wind turbines ugly.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sifton |first=Sam |date=2025-12-23 |title=Why Doesn’t Trump Like Wind Farms? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/23/briefing/why-doesnt-trump-like-wind-farms.html |access-date=2026-04-04 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Trump has also expressed concerns about the large percentage of the world's wind turbines being built in [[China]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Horton |first=Helena |last2=reporter |first2=Helena Horton Environment |date=2025-07-28 |title=Tilting at windmills? Trump’s claims about turbines fact-checked |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2025/jul/28/are-trump-claims-about-wind-power-correct |access-date=2026-04-04 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Trump has criticized wind energy for being expensive and for not working without "massive subsidies".<ref name="al">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/the-fix/wp/2016/05/26/theres-a-lot-to-unpack-in-donald-trumps-answers-about-energy-policy/|title=There's a lot to unpack in just one of Donald Trump's answers about energy policy|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=May 27, 2016}}</ref> He added, "windmills are killing hundreds and hundreds of eagles. One of the most beautiful, one of the most treasured birds—and they're killing them by the hundreds and nothing happens,"<ref name="al"/> a claim rated as "mostly false" by PolitiFact since best estimates indicate that about one hundred [[golden eagle]]s are killed each year by wind turbine blades.<ref>Jon Greenberg, [http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2016/may/31/donald-trump/trump-exaggerates-wind-turbine-eagle-deaths/ Trump inflates wind turbine eagle deaths], ''[[PolitiFact]]'' (May 31, 2016).</ref>

In his 2016 platform, Trump claimed that he will reduce bureaucracy which would then lead to greater innovation.<ref name="ep"/> His platform mentions "renewable energies", including "nuclear, wind and solar energy" in that regard but adds that he would not support those "to the exclusion of other energy".<ref name="ep"/>

Trump supports a higher [[Ethanol fuel in the United States|ethanol mandate]] (the amount of ethanol required by federal regulation to be blended into the U.S. gasoline supply).<ref>Timothy Cama, [https://thehill.com/policy/energy-environment/266339-trump-calls-for-higher-ethanol-mandate/ Trump calls for higher ethanol mandate], ''[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]' (January 19, 2016).''</ref> Trump vowed to protect the government's Renewable Fuel Standard and corn-based ethanol.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-09-15/trump-caught-between-corn-oil-interests-on-renewable-fuels|title=Trump Caught Between Corn, Oil Interests on Renewable Fuels|access-date=October 25, 2016|work=[[Bloomberg News]]|first=Jennifer|last=Dlouhy|date=September 15, 2016}}</ref>

===Wildlife conservation and animal welfare===
In October 2016, the [[Humane Society of the United States]] denounced Trump's campaign, saying that a "Trump presidency would be a threat to animals everywhere" and that he has "a team of advisors and financial supporters tied in with trophy hunting, puppy mills, factory farming, horse slaughter, and other abusive industries."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/299626-humane-society-legislative-fund-backs-clinton-launches-ad-against-trump/|title=Humane Society launches ad: Trump presidency a 'threat to animals everywhere'|last=Neidig|first=Harper|date=October 6, 2016|newspaper=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}</ref>

In February 2017, under the Trump administration, the [[U.S. Department of Agriculture]] (USDA) unexpectedly removed from its public website "all enforcement records related to [[horse soring]] and to [[animal welfare]] at dog breeding operations and other facilities."<ref name="Brulliard">Karin Brulliard, [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/animalia/wp/2017/02/09/usda-animal-welfare-records-purge-may-have-been-triggered-by-horse-industry-lawsuit/ USDA removed animal welfare reports from its site. A showhorse lawsuit may be why.], ''[[The Washington Post]]'' (February 9, 2017).</ref> The decision prompted criticism from animal welfare advocates (such as the [[Animal Welfare Institute]]), [[investigative journalist]]s, and some of the regulated industries (the [[Association of Zoos and Aquariums]] and the group [[Speaking of Research]] said that the move created an impression of non-transparency).<ref name="Brulliard"/>
