}}}}There are seven male and two female dormitories at Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology (DUET). The halls are as follows:

* ''[[Fazlur Rahman Khan]] Hall''<br>Male hall named after the famous architect and engineer Fazlur Rahman Khan. Provides accommodation and study facilities for students.
* ''[[Muhammad Qudrat-i-Khuda|Muhammad Qudrat-E-Khuda]] Hall''<br>Male hall named after scientist Dr. Muhammad Qudrat-E-Khuda, offering residence and common student amenities.
* [[Mukti Bahini|Shaheed Muktijoddha]] ''Hall''<br>Male hall honoring Bangladesh’s freedom fighters, with shared living and recreational spaces.
* ''[[Kazi Nazrul Islam]] Hall''<br>Male hall named after the national poet, providing modern residence facilities for students.
* ''[[Kazi Nazrul Islam]] Extension Hall''<br>Additional accommodation for Kazi Nazrul Islam Hall residents due to high demand.
* ''[[Marie Curie]] Hall''<br>Female hall named after scientist Marie Curie, with living spaces and common facilities.
* ''[[Marie Curie]] Extension Hall''<br>Extra accommodation for Marie Curie Hall residents.
* ''[[Tajuddin Ahmad|Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad]] Hall''<br>Male hall named after Bangladesh’s first prime minister, offering residential and study facilities.

=== Sports facilities ===
DUET provides students with access to three main playgrounds, one of which is located at the second campus along with one smaller playground, a basketball court, and a volleyball court, ensuring space for various sporting activities.<ref>{{cite web |title=DUET opens campus craft project event |url=https://thedailycampus.com/engineering-university/134717/%E0%A6%A1%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%83%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%B2-%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%85%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B7%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4 |website=The Daily Campus |language=bn |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref> The sports facilities at DUET include amenities for [[association football|football]], [[cricket]],<ref>{{cite news |title=KU wins by 34 runs against DUET in inter‑university cricket match |url=https://www.risingbd.com/campus/news/541814 |work=RisingBD |language=bn |date=8 February 2024 |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref> [[volleyball]], [[basketball]], [[table tennis]], [[carrom]], and [[badminton]]. Additionally, DUET organizes yearly inter-department and inter-hall tournaments.<ref>{{cite news |title=DUET holds inter‑departmental football tournament final |url=https://www.protidinersangbad.com/sports/145696/protidinersangbad.com/national/238954 |work=Protidiner Sangbad |language=bn |date=23 October 2018 |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=DUET wins via tiebreaker in inter‑university football match |url=https://www.prothomalo.com/sports/football/dglza5c4vr |work=Prothom Alo |language=bn |date=30 November 2024 |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Inauguration of DUET inter‑department football competition 2024 |url=https://www.tritiyamatra.com/news/19554/%E0%A6%A1%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%83%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%97-%E0%A6%AB%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%B2-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A7%A8%E0%A7%A6%E0%A7%A8%E0%A7%AA-%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%8B%E0+A6%A7%E0%A6%A8 |website=Tritiyo Matra |language=bn |date=9 December 2024 |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref>

===Students Complex===
[[File:Student Complex Building.jpg|right|thumb|Students Complex Building]]
The DUET Student Complex is a building where students come together for various activities. It houses spaces for different [[Club (organization)|clubs]] such as the English Language Club, Robotics Club, DUET Journal Association, and Srijonee. The complex also has the Shaheed Mostofa [[Cafeteria]]. There are meeting areas for students. It includes a [[gym]]nasium.<ref>{{cite web |title=Journey of DUET Journalists' Association |url=https://thedailycampus.com/engineering-university/35397/%E0%A6%A1%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A6%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE |website=The Daily Campus |language=bn |date=24 December 2019 |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nawroj.com.bd/%E0%A6%A1%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%83%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%A0/ |script-title=bn:ডুয়েটের সাংস্কৃতিক সংগঠন 'সৃজনী'র নতুন কমিটি ঘোষণা, নেতৃত্বে ওয়াসিম - রাজন - নওরোজ |website=নওরোজ |date=26 October 2024 |language=bn |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref>

===Computer Center===
The Computer Center is responsible for developing and managing the university's [[computing]] and [[Network hardware|networking]] infrastructure, providing essential support for undergraduate and postgraduate [[teaching]], [[learning]], and [[research]] across all departments. It oversees central internet facilities, including high-speed connections and campus-wide Wi-Fi, and manages central email and web servers to facilitate electronic communication both within and outside the university. All departments, offices, halls, and residential areas are interconnected through a [[fiber-optic]] LAN backbone. The center also handles the creation of identity cards for students, faculty, and staff. Its primary objectives include designing and maintaining [[IT infrastructure]], fostering a conducive computing environment for learning and research, developing human resources through training programs, and actively pursuing advanced IT research to create knowledge-based products and services.<ref>{{cite web |title=Computer Center |url=https://www.duet.ac.bd/office/computer-center |website=Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology |access-date=2025-09-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Chandpur Science & Technology University's first VC Prof. Nasim, Director of DUET Computer Center |url=https://www.jugantor.com/campus/389103 |work=Jugantor |language=bn |date=30 January 2021 |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref>

===Political and unregistered organizations===
Since September 2024, political organizations, regional organizations, and all types of unregistered student organizations have been banned at DUET.<ref>{{cite news |script-title=bn:ডুয়েটে নিষিদ্ধ হলো ছাত্র রাজনীতি |url=https://jamuna.tv/news/560698 |work=Jamuna TV |date=4 September 2024 |access-date=5 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |script-title=bn:ডুয়েটে রাজনীতি করলেই শাস্তি |url=https://www.somoynews.tv/news/2024-09-04/9ZxuNv2y |work=Somoy News |language=bn |date=4 September 2024 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |script-title=bn:আগামী ২১ নভেম্বর ডুয়েট ছাত্রদলের সাবেকদের মিলনমেলা |url=https://dailynayadiganta.com/bangladesh/education-campus/pcxvJLkCjqSI |work=Daily Naya Diganta |language=bn |date=27 October 2025 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |script-title=bn:ডুয়েট ছাত্রদলের সাবেকদের মিলনমেলার নিবন্ধন চলছে |url=https://www.somoynews.tv/news/2025-10-28/BCGtTx2K |work=Somoy News |language=bn |date=28 October 2025 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

* DUET Photographic Society: Focuses on photography skills through workshops and exhibitions.
* DUET Literature Society: The DUET Literature Society, a sub-committee of Srijoni, promotes literary activities on campus through classic literature posts, weekly reading sessions, and open bookshelves. Its goal is to enrich DUET's reading culture.<ref>{{cite web |title=DUET Society |url=https://duetsociety.org/ |accessdate=25 November 2025}}</ref>
* DUET Adventure Club: A student organization that promotes physical fitness, mental resilience, and exploration through structured tours, mountaineering expeditions, and outdoor skill-building activities for students interested in nature and travel.

===Journalism Club===
* DUET Journalist Association (DJA): Teaches journalism, writing, and reporting. Members cover campus news and develop media skills.<ref>{{cite web |script-title=bn:ডুয়েট সাংবাদিক সমিতির যাত্রা |url=https://thedailycampus.com/engineering-university/35397/%E0%A6%A1%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A6%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95-%E0%A6%B8%E0%AE%BE%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE |website=The Daily Campus |date=2019-12-24 |access-date=2025-11-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |script-title=bn:ডুয়েট সাংবাদিক সমিতির সভাপতি |url=https://www.news24bd.tv/details/141730 |website=News24BD |access-date=2025-11-05}}</ref>

===Voluntary clubs===
* Swajan, DUET : DUET Voluntary Blood Donor Organization: Organizes blood donation events and promotes voluntary donation.
* DUET Blood Donation Society (DBDS): Conducts regular blood donation programs in support of hospitals and patients.
* DUET CR Forum: A student organization at DUET that represents class representatives, promoting student engagement, leadership, and coordination between students and faculty.

===Religious organizations===
* DUET Dawah Circle (DDC): Works to promote Islamic education and values among students by encouraging ethical living, social responsibility, and personal development based on Islamic principles, while maintaining respect for followers of all religions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DUET Dawah Circle (DDC) |url=https://www.duet.ac.bd/clubs-communities/24/duet-dawah-circle-ddc |website=Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology |access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref>
* Bani Archana Sangshad (DUET): Supports spiritual and moral learning for personal growth.<ref>{{cite web |title=Clubs & Communities at DUET |url=https://www.duet.ac.bd/clubs-communities |access-date=24 October 2025}}</ref>
* Buddha Chatro Kalyan Parishad (BSWA): Established in 2004, it is the sole organization for Buddhist students at DUET, focusing on student welfare, religious and cultural activities, and social service.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buddha Chatro Kalyan Parishad |url=https://www.duet.ac.bd/clubs-communities/23/buddha-chatro-kalyan-parishad |website=Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology |access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref>

== Administration ==
===Top administrators===
#* [[Chancellor (education)|Chancellor]]: Holds a ceremonial role, presides over major events such as convocations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Top Administrator – Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology, Gazipur |url=https://www.duet.ac.bd/admin-bodies/top-administrator |website=Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology |language=en |access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref>
#* [[Vice-Chancellor]]: Acts as the university's chief executive, responsible for overall administration and academic affairs.
#* [[Pro-vice-chancellor]]:  Assist the vice-chancellor in specific areas such as academic planning, research, or student affairs.
# Administrative Bodies:
#* Syndicate: Formulates policies, approves budgets, and ensures the smooth functioning of the university's operations.
#* Finance Committee: Manages financial resources, monitors expenditures, and ensures financial transparency and accountability.
#* CASR (Committee for Academic and Student Regulations): Develops academic policies, oversees regulations, and maintains academic standards.
#* Planning and Development Committee:  Formulates strategic plans for the university's growth and development, including infrastructure projects and resource allocation.
#* Academic Council: Responsible for academic planning, curriculum design, program evaluation, and quality assurance.
#* [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of Faculties: Oversee the academic affairs of their respective faculties, including curriculum implementation and faculty development.
#* [[Head of college|Heads]] of Departments: Manage day-to-day operations within their departments, including academic programs, research initiatives, and faculty management.
#* [[Director (education)|Directors]]: Provide leadership for various academic and non-academic units, ensuring their effective functioning and alignment with the university's goals and objectives
[[File:Administrative Building at DUET.jpg|alt=Administrative Building at|thumb|Administrative Building]]

== Second campus ==
Dhaka University of Engineering and Technology (DUET) 2nd campus is an ongoing development project aimed at accommodating the growing number of students at DUET. Situated on Majhir Khola Rd, Gazipur, near to the DUET main campus, this expansion initiative includes the construction of various facilities such as the ICT Incubator Building, an academic building, and a student hall.<ref name="thedailycampus.com"/>
<gallery  heights="120" class="center">
File:Ariel views the second campus.jpg|Aerial view of the second campus
File:Bijoy 24 Hall.jpg|Bijoy 24 Hall, DUET
File:Second Campus Academic Buildng.jpg|Academic Building, DUET
</gallery>
The need for this expansion arises from the increasing student population, necessitating additional infrastructure to support academic activities effectively. The development plan extends beyond the current construction phase, with a master plan in place to further enlarge the campus by 2041. Once completed, the DUET 2nd campus will provide enhanced facilities and resources to meet the educational needs of students, contributing to the overall academic excellence of DUET. DUET administration has started academic activities at the second campus in January 2025.<ref>{{cite web |script-title=bn:শিক্ষাক্ষেত্রে নতুন উদ্যোগ |url=https://www.dailyporibar.com/education/news/9598 |website=Dainik Paribar |date= |access-date=21 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |script-title=bn:ডুয়েটে বিজয় ২৪ হল উদ্বোধন |url=https://www.dailynayadiganta.com/dhaka/19686373/%E0%A6%A1%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9C%E0%A7%9F-%E0%A7%A8%E0%A7%AA-%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%B2-%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%A8 |newspaper=[[Daily Naya Diganta]] |date=20 January 2025 |access-date=23 January 2025 |language=bn}}</ref>

== Dhaka Engineering University School ==
[[File:Dhaka University School.png|thumb|left|Campus view of Dhaka Engineering University School]]
Dhaka Engineering University School is a primary and secondary level educational institution adjacent to the campus of the Dhaka University of Engineering and Technology (DUET) in the Bhurulia area of Gazipur district, Bangladesh. It was established in 1994 when DUET was the Bangladesh Institute of Technology (BIT), Dhaka. The school operates in close association with the DUET academic environment and follows government-approved education board curricula. It places importance on discipline, moral education, and overall academic development.
<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Dhaka Engineering University School Official Facebook Page
 |url=https://www.facebook.com/duetschoolofficial/
 |website=Facebook
 |access-date=28 January 2026
}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Dhaka Engineering University School Institute Information
 |url=https://locator.eduportalbd.com/institutes/?ins=130692
 |website=EduPortal Bangladesh
 |access-date=28 January 2026
}}</ref>

The school mainly serves the children of DUET students and staff, offering a convenient learning environment within the university area. As an institution connected to DUET, it regularly takes part in co-curricular activities such as sports events and cultural programs, which support the physical, social, and mental growth of students.

 |title=Dhaka Engineering University School EIIN Information

'''Donald Gilbert Shelby''' (born May 27, 1947)<ref name="whereborn">{{cite news | title = Bio: Don Shelby | publisher = [[WCCO-TV|WCCO]] | url = http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/personality/don-shelby/ | accessdate = 2010-11-22 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20101115110910/http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/personality/don-shelby/ | archivedate = 2010-11-15 }}</ref> is a retired American journalist who was a [[news anchor]] on [[WCCO-TV]] in [[Minneapolis, Minnesota]] for much of his career. He is regarded as an experienced investigative journalist, as his work has earned two [[Peabody award]]s and three [[Emmy Award]]s.<ref name="whereborn" /><ref name="goodage"/><ref>[https://www.twincities.com/2010/09/25/wcco-tvs-don-shelby-awarded-best-anchor-regional-emmy/ WCCO-TV’s Don Shelby awarded ‘best anchor’ regional Emmy]. Twin Cities.com Pioneer Press, September 25, 2010</ref> He also has won the other three top journalism awards of the United States, including the Columbia DuPont Citation, the Scripps-Howard Award and the [[Society of Professional Journalists]] Distinguished Service Award.<ref name="whereborn"/>

==Early life==

Shelby was born and raised in [[Royerton, Indiana]], near Muncie.<ref name="goodage"/><ref name="Signoff">Gustafson, Amy Carlson - [https://www.twincities.com/2010/11/13/don-shelby-prepares-to-sign-off-on-32-year-career-at-wcco-tv/ Don Shelby prepares to sign off on 32-year career at WCCO-TV]. Twin Cities.com Pioneer Press, November 13, 2010</ref> He was a high school basketball standout.<ref name="Signoff"/> He attended the [[University of Cincinnati]] for two years, but left to enlist in the [[United States Air Force]].<ref name="Signoff"/><ref name="lastdon">Gihring, Tim - [https://www.minnesotamonthly.com/lifestyle/the-last-don/ The Last Don]. Minnesota Monthly, October 22, 2009</ref>   He met his wife, Barbara, when he was stationed at Bolling Air Force base in Washington, D.C., where Barbara worked as an administrative assistant.<ref name="goodage"/><ref name="Signoff"/> Shelby was honorably discharged in 1972 after serving four years.<ref name="Signoff"/>
He worked in [[Charleston, South Carolina]] and [[Houston, Texas]] before arriving in Minneapolis.<ref name="Signoff"/>

==WCCO-TV==
Shelby joined [[WCCO-TV]] in the summer of 1978 as a news reporter.<ref name="Signoff"/> After continued work as a reporter, Shelby began assuming anchor responsibilities in greater capacity, eventually assuming the primary anchor chair from [[Dave Moore (newscaster)|Dave Moore]]. Shelby was the chief architect behind WCCO's "I-Team" segment, which spotlighted current issues, both local and on a larger world scale, with rigorous investigative journalism. After suffering a mild stroke in early 2004, Shelby returned to news reading duties by the end of that year. In 2009, Shelby was reported to make US$1 Million, before taking a 10% pay cut in 2010 to help WCCO trim costs.<ref name="lastdon"/> Shelby retired from television after his final WCCO-TV newscast on November 22, 2010.<ref name="whenretired">{{cite news | title = Recap: Don Shelby's Final Newscast | work = ? | publisher = [[WCCO-TV|WCCO]] | url = http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2010/11/22/recap-don-shelby-retires-final-newscast/ | accessdate = 2010-11-22}}</ref><ref name="Signoff"/>

During a Minnesota-themed segment of [[The Late Show with David Letterman]], the camera cut to the WCCO newsroom. Don Shelby turned to WCCO co-anchor Amelia Santaniello and said, "Amelia, I have a gopher in my pants and his name is Carlos."<ref>[https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/a-look-at-minnesotans-long-history-on-letterman/ A Look At Minnesotans' Long History On Letterman]. CBS News, May 20, 2015</ref>

=== War and conflict reporting ===
Shelby covered numerous international conflicts as a correspondent, including the [[Yom Kippur War]] in 1973 and the [[Iraq War]]. Major General Richard Nash, commander of forces in the southern half of Iraq, referred to Don as "our [[Ernie Pyle]]."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Don Shelby |url=https://nationallyspeaking.com/cm-expert/don-shelby/ |access-date=2024-10-12 |website=Nationally Speaking |language=en-US}}</ref>

==="Good To Know"===
In February 2006, Shelby began hosting a series of video essay segments entitled "In The Know" (later renamed "Good To Know"), during the station's 10:00 newscast.<ref>[https://tcbmag.com/don-shelby-is-out-standing-in-his-field/ Don Shelby is Out Standing in His Field]. Twin Cities Business, October 11, 2010</ref> These segments sometimes touched on political, religious and other topics, usually with the same pointed journalistic style of Shelby's earlier "I-Team" efforts.

=== "Project Energy" ===
In April, 2006, Shelby's environmental series "Project Energy" began airing on WCCO.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Press |first=Amy Carlson Gustafson {{!}} Special to the Pioneer |date=2010-11-13 |title=Don Shelby prepares to sign off on 32-year career at WCCO-TV |url=https://www.twincities.com/2010/11/13/don-shelby-prepares-to-sign-off-on-32-year-career-at-wcco-tv/ |access-date=2024-10-12 |website=Twin Cities |language=en-US}}</ref> The regular news segment focused on climate change, energy consumption, and conservation was one of the earliest examples of local broadcast journalism focused on climate change.

==WCCO-AM radio==
From 2000 through 2009, Shelby undertook a dual responsibility of hosting an afternoon radio show on [[WCCO (AM)]] which ended at 6:00, immediately after which he anchored the TV newscast (also [[simulcast]] on radio). He partnered on the radio with WCCO radio news anchor [[Jeff McKinney]]. In June 2009, ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' sideline reporter [[Michele Tafoya]] took over the 3:30&nbsp;p.m. to 6:00&nbsp;p.m. time slot, with Shelby moving to the early afternoon drive, then sharing the microphone with Michelle from 3:00&nbsp;p.m. to 3:30&nbsp;p.m.<ref name="wcco2009">Gustafson, Amy Carlson  - [https://www.twincities.com/2009/04/19/michele-tafoya-gets-wcco-am-drive-time-slot/ Michele Tafoya gets WCCO-AM drive-time slot]. TwinCities.com Pioneer Press, April 19, 2009</ref><ref name="michele">{{cite news | title = Bio: Michele Tafoya | work = Personalities | publisher = [[WCCO-AM]] | url = http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/personality/michele-tafoya/ | accessdate = 2010-11-22 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20101118082027/http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/personality/michele-tafoya/ | archivedate = 2010-11-18 }}</ref> Shelby's final radio show took place on December 11, 2009.<ref>Gustafson, Amy Carlson - [https://www.twincities.com/2009/12/06/after-nine-years-of-polite-conversation-don-shelby-will-switch-off-his-wcco-radio-mic-today/ After nine years of polite conversation, Don Shelby will switch off his WCCO radio mic today]. Twin Cities.com Pioneer Press, December 6, 2009</ref><ref>[https://www.twincities.com/2009/12/11/don-shelby-signs-off-on-wcco-am-radio/ Don Shelby signs off on WCCO-AM radio]. Twin Cities.com Pioneer Press, December 11, 2009</ref>

==Community work==
Shelby has played an active role in the preservation and maintenance of the [[Mississippi River]]. Through his WCCO-TV segment entitled "Project Energy", Shelby has investigated energy conservation, renewable energy, and alternative fuels.<ref name="projectenergy">{{cite news |title=University of Minnesota Initiative for Renewable Energy and the Environment Annual Research Symposium |publisher=World Changing Twin Cities |url=http://www.worldchanging.com/local/twincities/archives/005486.html |accessdate=2010-11-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110507043222/http://www.worldchanging.com/local/twincities/archives/005486.html |archivedate=2011-05-07 }}</ref>  Shelby has also given his time as an on-air representative for a number of pledge drives on behalf of the local PBS station TPT (KTCA), as well as narrated the third installment of "Lost Twin Cities", a TPT produced documentary. He appeared in "[[America Unearthed]]".<ref>Pratt, Anna (March 19, 2022) "[https://www.startribune.com/america-unearthed-host-is-history-sleuth/250822791/ A real-life 'Da Vinci Code']", ''[[Star Tribune]]''. Retrieved August 9, 2022.</ref>

==Stage acting==
Don appeared in the Lab Theater's production of Rocky Horror, appearing with numerous Guthrie actors in a performance of 8 at the Varsity Theater in 2011.<ref name="theat">[https://www.broadwayworld.com/minneapolis/article/Don-Shelby-and-Nancy-Nelson-to-Perform-LOVE-LETTERS-at-Chanhassen-Dinner-Theaters-This-November-20221006 Don Shelby and Nancy Nelson to Perform LOVE LETTERS at Chanhassen Dinner Theaters This November]. Broadway World Minneapolis.St, Paul, October 6, 2022</ref>  He was a featured actor in Safe at Home at the Mixed Blood Theatre.<ref name="theat"/> He has performed the character of Mark Twain more than 200 times, in shows at performing arts centers throughout the state of Minnesota.<ref name="theat"/> He also has performed as Mark Twain in New Orleans and aboard the [[Delta Queen]] Riverboat on the Mississippi River in St. Louis.<ref name="theat"/> In November 2022, Shelby began acting in “Love Letters” with Nancy Nelson at Chanhassen Dinner Theatres.<ref>Preston Rohan - [https://www.startribune.com/this-just-in-don-shelby-and-nancy-nelson-exchange-love-letters-onstage/600220910/ This just in: Don Shelby and Nancy Nelson exchange 'Love Letters' onstage]. Star Tribune, November 1, 2022</ref> The run was so successful that it returned the following February and is slated for a third run as of October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-12 |title='Love Letters' returns to Chanhassen Dinner Theatres |url=https://www.kare11.com/article/news/local/kare11-saturday/love-letters-chanhassen-dinner-theatres/89-36448cf5-d284-4412-89ec-21ec4f974e33 |access-date=2024-10-12 |website=kare11.com |language=en-US}}</ref> It ran again in the fall of 2025 and is exprected to return again in February 2026.<ref>Wild, Stephi - [https://www.broadwayworld.com/minneapolis/article/Don-Shelby-and-Nancy-Nelson-Bring-LOVE-LETTERS-to-Chanhassen-Dinner-Theatres-20250604 Don Shelby and Nancy Nelson Bring LOVE LETTERS to Chanhassen Dinner Theatres] Broadwayworld.com, June 4, 2025</ref>

==Personal life==
Known to many in the Minnesota community as a "jack-of-all-trades," Shelby has many hobbies, including, among other things, [[beekeeping]]. Shelby has been an enthusiastic fan of women's basketball. He is a resident of [[Excelsior, Minnesota]], in a farmhouse certified [[LEED Platinum]].<ref name="leed">{{Cite web|url=https://shelby637.rssing.com/chan-45965238/article29.html|title=Don Shelby Gets Energy Efficient In His Own Home|date=March 1, 2012|via=WCCO-TV}}</ref><ref>[https://www.minnesotamonthly.com/archive/home-green-home-don-shelbys-sustainable-house-makes-a-statement/ Home Green Home: Don Shelby’s sustainable house makes a statement]. Minnesota Monthly, march 14, 2012</ref><ref>Hewett, Chris - [https://www.startribune.com/revisiting-don-shelby-s-green-dream-home-in-excelsior/572843602/ 8 years after building his green dream home, Don Shelby strives to go even greener]. Star Tribune, October 24, 2020</ref> His eldest daughter is the novelist and short story writer Ashley Shelby.

===Author===

His first book, ''The Season Never Ends: Wins, Losses, and the Wisdom of the Game'', was published on August 30, 2011. It features a foreword by former [[University of Minnesota]] men's basketball head coach [[Tubby Smith]] and endorsements from NBA analyst [[Ahmad Rashad]] and author [[Will Weaver]].

===Health===

Shelby had two debilitating strokes in 2004, from which he recovered while he was still in his broadcasting career.<ref>Burger, Kevyn - [https://www.startribune.com/get-a-hobby-former-wcco-anchor-don-shelby-shows-us-why-older-people-need-one-or-five/600079991/ Get a hobby! Former WCCO anchor Don Shelby shows us why older people need one – or five]. Star Tribune, July 21, 2021</ref><ref>Justin, Neal - [https://www.startribune.com/shelby-ready-to-fade-to-black-ponders-life-out-of-cco-spotlight/107800989/ Shelby, ready to fade to black, ponders life out of 'CCO spotlight]. Star Tribune, November 14, 2010</ref> He had another stroke in 2021.<ref>Justin, Neal - [https://www.startribune.com/how-former-wcco-anchor-don-shelby-learned-to-speak-again/600155094 How former WCCO anchor Don Shelby learned to speak again] Star Tribune, March 12, 2022</ref> In 2016, Shelby shared his story of his recovery from alcohol addiction and reported being 36 years sober since 1980.<ref>David, Rebecca - [https://wjon.com/don-shelby-shares-his-recovery-from-alcohol-with-st-cloud-alano-society/ Don Shelby Shares His Recovery From Alcohol With St. Cloud Alano Society] WJON.com, September 16, 2016</ref>

===Shelby Knot===
{{main|Pratt knot}}
Shelby, in his time on television, popularized the [[Pratt knot|Pratt]] necktie knot, to the extent that it is sometimes referred to as the "Shelby Knot" or "Pratt-Shelby." The knot was created by [[Jerry Pratt]], an employee of the [[US Chamber of Commerce]], who taught it to Shelby in 1986.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=http://www.people.com/people/archive/article/0,,20121319,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304071808/www.people.com/people/archive/article/0,,20121319,00.html|url-status=dead|title=Taking a Tip from a Dapper Fan, Anchorman Don Shelby Makes News with the Knot in His Necktie|date=October 2, 1989|website=People|archive-date=2016-03-04}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/08/30/garden/as-neckwear-goes-this-knot-s-news.html|title=As Neckwear Goes, This Knot's News|first=William E.|last=Schmidt|work=The New York Times |date=August 30, 1989|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref> The knot was considered at the time to be "the first new knot for men in over 50 years" by [[the New York Times]]. It is speculated that the knot had been in use for a time, but the knot simply had not been documented until Don Shelby made it famous by the help of Jerry Pratt and the Minneapolis clothier Kingford Bavender.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto2"/> Kingford Bavender is considered to have coined the term the "Shelby" knot.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://tcbmag.com/king-brothers-and-don-shelby-tied-to-a-knot/|title=King Brothers and Don Shelby: Tied to a Knot|date=June 2, 2013|website=Twin Cities Business}}</ref>

In honor of the history of the Shelby Knot and Don Shelby, a bespoke clothier company by the name of King Brothers Clothiers partnered with Mr. Shelby and launched the Shelby Knot Collection of ties in the spring of 2013. Together, Don Shelby and King Brothers Clothiers, selected the designs of the ties that reflected Don's tastes.<ref name="auto1"/>
